definition_zh: 运送；传送；传达；转让（财产）
definition_en: to carry people or goods from one place to another, to communicate an idea or feeling, or to transfer property legally
core_image: 一条从甲地通向乙地的通道，东西顺着通道被带到另一头
scene: 港口仓库里，最后一箱零件停在装卸通道口。 The workers conveyed the last crate of parts to the back of the truck, which then left for the customer's factory.
sceneCN: 这里 convey 是「运送、传送」（第 1 个义项：把东西从一处运到另一处）；句意：工人把最后一箱零件运到货车尾部，货车随后开往客户的工厂。

pos.zh: 运送；传送；传达；转让（财产）

derivatives.zh: 运输；交通工具；财产转让

senses.title: Physical transport: carry goods or people
senses.titleCN: 实体运送：把人和货带到另一处
senses.definition: to take goods, people, or objects from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 把货物、人或物件从一处带到另一处
senses.example: The ferry conveys passengers across the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 渡轮把乘客送到海湾对岸。
senses.why: Convey was built on Latin com- 'with' + via 'road'. The first image is a person travelling along a road with something in hand, so the basic sense is physical carriage.
senses.whyCN: convey 由拉丁语 com-“一起”+ via“道路”构成。最初的画面是一个人带着东西沿路同行，因此最基本的义项就是实体运送。

senses.title: Communication: make meaning travel
senses.definition: to communicate an idea, meaning, or feeling to someone
senses.definitionCN: 把观念、含义或情感传递给别人
senses.example: A chart can convey a trend faster than a paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 一张图表比一段文字更快地传达趋势。
senses.why: The road becomes abstract: the message is what travels, and the listener is the destination. Language, image or gesture is now the channel.
senses.whyCN: 道路变成了抽象的：在路上的是信息，听者就是终点。语言、图像或手势此时充当通道。

senses.title: Transmission: carry sound, signals, or energy
senses.titleCN: 传输：运送声音、信号或能量
senses.definition: to carry sound, electricity, light, or a signal from one point to another
senses.definitionCN: 把声音、电、光或信号从一点输送到另一点
senses.example: The pipes convey hot water to every floor.
senses.exampleCN: 这些管道把热水送到每一层楼。
senses.why: A pipe or wire is a road for energy. The same 'carry along' structure is applied to water, current and light, with no meaning involved.
senses.whyCN: 管子或电线就是能量的道路。同样的“沿路带过去”结构被用在热水、电流和光上，此时不涉及任何意义。

senses.title: Legal transfer: hand over ownership
senses.titleCN: 法律转让：把所有权交出去
senses.definition: to transfer ownership of land or property from one person to another by legal document
senses.definitionCN: 通过法律文件把土地或财产的所有权从一人转给另一人
senses.example: The deed conveys the land to the buyer.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据把土地转让给买方。
senses.why: In law, property travels from one owner to another, and the document is the road. Old French conveier already meant 'to hand over, transfer', so the legal sense keeps the original handover.
senses.whyCN: 在法律上，财产从一个所有者“走”到另一个所有者，文件就是那条路。古法语 conveier 本就有“交出、转让”义，因此法律义保留了最初的“交接”动作。

senses.title: Escort: conduct a person somewhere
senses.definition: to escort or conduct a person to a place, especially in a formal or official situation
senses.definitionCN: 把人护送到某地，尤用于正式或公务场合
senses.example: Two officers conveyed the witness to the courthouse.
senses.exampleCN: 两名警官把证人送到法院。
senses.why: This is the oldest English sense, 'to escort or conduct'. The thing carried is a person, and the carrying is protected movement along a route.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语最早的义项“护送、引领”。被带过去的是一个人，这种“带”是沿路线进行的受保护移动。

senses.title: Relay a message for someone else
senses.titleCN: 转达：替别人把话带过去
senses.definition: to pass on someone else's message, thanks, or greetings to a third person
senses.definitionCN: 把别人的消息、谢意或问候转给第三方
senses.example: Please convey my thanks to the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 请把我的谢意转达给整个团队。
senses.why: Here the speaker is only the channel: another person's words travel through you to a third person. The road image is now social.
senses.whyCN: 这里说话者只是通道：另一个人的话经过你到达第三个人。道路意象此时变成了人际层面的。

senses.title: Imply: give an impression without saying it
senses.titleCN: 暗示：不说出口也让人感到
senses.definition: to give a feeling or impression indirectly, through design, tone, or atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 通过设计、语气或氛围间接给人某种感觉或印象
senses.example: The empty white walls convey a sense of calm.
senses.exampleCN: 空白的白墙给人一种平静感。
senses.why: The signal is not stated in words but still reaches the viewer. Convey covers this because the impression travels through the design, not through a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 信号没有用文字说出，却仍然到达观看者。convey 能覆盖这一层，因为印象是通过设计而不是句子传过去的。

senses.title: Succeed in making oneself understood
senses.titleCN: 讲清楚：让意思真正到达
senses.definition: to succeed in making a meaning understood, especially when this is difficult
senses.definitionCN: 成功让别人理解自己的意思，尤指这件事并不容易时
senses.example: She could not convey how urgent the problem was.
senses.exampleCN: 她没能让别人明白这个问题有多紧急。
senses.why: The verb here marks arrival rather than departure: the meaning actually reaches the listener. The road metaphor adds a success test — a message that never lands has not been conveyed.
senses.whyCN: 这里的动词标记的是“到达”而非“出发”：意思确实抵达了听者。道路比喻因此多了一层成功检验——没有落地的信息不算 convey 成功。

intro.en: Convey is a road word. Latin via 'road' sits inside it, and English first used it for escorting a person, then for carrying goods, messages, signals, and finally legal ownership.
intro.cn: convey 是一个“道路”词。拉丁语 via“道路”藏在里面；英语先用它表示护送人，再表示运送货物、传递消息与信号，最后用于法律上的所有权转移。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'to escort, accompany, conduct'. The sense 'to carry, transport' is recorded from the late 14c.
items.cn: 最早记录于 13 世纪晚期的英语，意为“护送、陪同、引领”；“运送、运输”义见于 14 世纪晚期。

items.en: From Old French conveier 'to escort, conduct, guide' (12c.; Modern French convoyer), which also meant 'to hand over, transfer'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 conveier（12 世纪）“护送、引领、带路”，现代法语作 convoyer；它同时有“交出、转让”义。

items.en: *Conviare 'to accompany on the way' = com- 'with' + viare 'to travel', from Latin via 'road, way'.
items.cn: 俗拉丁语 *conviare“在路上同行”= com-“一起”+ viare“行走”，后者来自拉丁语 via“道路”。

items.en: Latin via is traced to PIE *wegh- 'to go, carry in a vehicle', the root behind way, wagon, vehicle and voyage. The reconstruction is standard, though the intermediate form is generally accepted rather than proven.
items.cn: 拉丁语 via 被追溯到原始印欧语 *wegh-“走、用车载运”，也是 way、wagon、vehicle、voyage 的词根。这一重构是通行说法，中间形式属于一般认为是，而非确证。

items.en: The escort sense is now formal or archaic. The living senses are transport, communicate, transmit and legal transfer; convoy, voyage and previous keep the road image as separate words.
items.cn: “护送”义现在偏正式或古旧。仍在使用的义项是运送、传达、传输和法律转让；convoy、voyage、previous 作为独立词保留着同一条“道路”意象。

items.en: Convey and convince are different histories. Convey goes back to via 'road' and moves goods, messages, signals or property from one end to the other; convince goes back to vincere 'conquer' and wins a mind with evidence. Convey never means 'persuade', and convince never means 'carry'.
items.cn: convey 与 convince 是两条不同的词源线。convey 出自 via“道路”，把货物、消息、信号或财产从一端送到另一端；convince 出自 vincere“战胜”，用证据赢下一个头脑。convey 从不表示“说服”，convince 从不表示“运送、传递”。

note.en: The first group shares the road-and-carry shape; the second group splits the idea into transport, meaning, signal and legal transfer.
note.cn: 第一组共享“道路＋带过去”的词形与词源；第二组把这一概念分成运送、含义、信号和法律转让。

entries.definition: a group of vehicles or ships travelling together, usually for protection. It is the noun cousin of convey.
entries.definitionCN: 车队或船队，通常为保护而结伴同行；是 convey 的名词同族词。

entries.definition: the act of carrying something, a vehicle, or the legal transfer of property.
entries.definitionCN: 运送行为、交通工具，或财产的合法转让。

entries.definition: to make someone believe something. It shares the con- and conv- shape but comes from vincere 'to conquer', not via 'road': convey carries something, convince wins a mind.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人相信某事。它同样以 con- 和 conv- 开头，但来自 vincere“战胜”，而不是 via“道路”：convey 运送东西，convince 赢下头脑。

entries.definition: to move goods or people by vehicle. It covers only the physical sense, not communication.
entries.definitionCN: 用交通工具运送货物或人。它只覆盖实体运送，不表示传达。

entries.definition: to make information or feelings understood. It focuses on the message, not on carrying objects.
entries.definitionCN: 让信息或情感被理解。它聚焦于信息，而不是搬运物体。

entries.definition: to send out signals, sound, or disease. It is more technical than convey and often one-way.
entries.definitionCN: 发送信号、声音或传播疾病。它比 convey 更技术化，常是单向的。

entries.definition: to move something from one place, account, or owner to another. It overlaps the legal sense of convey.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从一处、一个账户或一个所有者转到另一处。它与 convey 的法律义重叠。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: com- 'with' + via 'road', with convoy, voyage, deviate and obvious in the same Latin family.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：com-“一起”+ via“道路”，convoy、voyage、deviate、obvious 都在同一个拉丁词族。

normal.en: com- 'with' + via 'road' = to go along the road with something. The word still carries that road inside it.
normal.cn: com-“一起”+ via“道路”=带着东西沿路同行。这个词内部至今藏着那条路。

normal.en: Convoy, voyage, deviate and obvious all contain via 'road': travelling together, a journey, turning off the road, and being in the way.
normal.cn: convoy、voyage、deviate、obvious 都含有 via“道路”：结伴同行、旅程、偏离道路、挡在路上。

normal.en: The oldest sense was 'escort a person', which is why convey can still be used for taking a witness to court.
normal.cn: 最早的义项是“护送一个人”，所以 convey 至今仍可用于把证人送到法庭。

normal.en: A deed conveys property in the same way a truck conveys goods: both hand something over to another side.
normal.cn: 契约 convey 财产，和卡车 convey 货物是同一种结构：都把东西交到另一端。

normal.en: Please convey my thanks is the social branch: you are the road along which someone else's words travel.
normal.cn: “please convey my thanks”是人际分支：你就是别人的话所走的那条路。

abstract.en: Picture a pipe running from one building to another. Goods, water, electricity or words can all be put into it; convey is the fact that they reach the far end.
abstract.cn: 想象一根管道从一栋楼通向另一栋楼。货物、水、电或话语都可以放进去；convey 就是“它们到达另一头”这件事。

abstract.en: The same channel can be physical, verbal or legal. Only the cargo changes — boxes, meanings, current, or ownership.
abstract.cn: 同一条通道可以是实体的、语言的或法律的。变的只是货物——箱子、含义、电流或所有权。

abstract.en: A message that never reaches anyone is only sent, not conveyed. The word quietly asks whether the far end received it.
abstract.cn: 没有到达任何人的信息只是“发出”，不算 conveyed。这个词暗暗追问：那一头真的收到了吗？

examples.en: The old pipeline still conveys water to the village.
examples.cn: 那条老管道仍在给村子输水。

examples.en: Her silence conveyed more than any explanation.
examples.cn: 她的沉默比任何解释都说明了更多东西。

examples.en: The seller conveyed the title to the buyer last week.
examples.cn: 卖方上周把所有权转让给了买方。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯为”——肯为你跑一趟，把东西和话都带到 → convey 运送、传达

root: 拉丁语 com-“一起、伴随”+ via“道路”，字面义“沿路同行、带过去”，核心是“让东西顺着通道到达另一处”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of convey, all one road image: goods, meaning, energy, property, a person, a message, an impression, and finally a meaning that actually arrives.
sensesIntro.cn: convey 的八个义项都是同一幅道路图：货物、含义、能量、财产、一个人、一句托付的话、一种暗示，以及最后“意思真的到达了”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something is carried along a channel from one end to the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物顺着一条通道，从一端被带到另一端。

branches.en: CHANNEL: goods and energy travel along a physical route.
branches.cn: 通道：货物与能量沿实体路线前进。

branches.en: MEANING: a message travels through words or images, and convey also marks that it arrived.
branches.cn: 含义：信息通过文字或图像旅行，而 convey 也标记它确实抵达了。

branches.en: OWNERSHIP: legal handover is the road image applied to property.
branches.cn: 所有权：法律交接就是把道路意象用在财产上。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the oldest English sense, escorting a person along a route.
branches.cn: 人：英语最早的义项，沿路线护送一个人。

branches.en: IMPLICIT: greetings relayed through a person, and impressions carried by design.
branches.cn: 间接：经人转达的问候，以及由设计携带的印象。

intro.en: Convey takes its Latin parts from via; English itself only adds -ance, -or and -able. The prefix con- belongs to the frozen Latin verb, not to a live English rule.
intro.cn: convey 的拉丁成分来自 via；英语本身只加 -ance、-or、-able。前缀 con- 属于凝固的拉丁动词，不是活的英语构词规则。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on via 'road': voyage, deviate, obvious, trivial and previous all describe movement along or off a way.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 via“道路”上：voyage、deviate、obvious、trivial、previous 都描述沿路或离路的移动。

items.meaning: the act of transporting; a vehicle; the legal transfer of property
items.meaningCN: 运送；交通工具；财产转让（-ance 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: The conveyance of the goods took two days.
items.exampleCN: 货物的运送花了两天。

items.meaning: a person or machine that carries things; a moving belt in a factory
items.meaningCN: 运送者；传送带（-or 表示做该动作的人或物）
items.example: Boxes move along the conveyor to the loading dock.
items.exampleCN: 箱子沿传送带移到装货口。

items.meaning: able to be carried or legally transferred
items.meaningCN: 可运送的；可转让的（-able 表示“能够被……”）
items.example: The right is conveyable only with the land.
items.exampleCN: 这项权利只能随土地一起转让。

items.meaning: the legal work of transferring property from one owner to another
items.meaningCN: 不动产转让事务（-ing 构成行业或过程名词）
items.example: The lawyer specialises in conveyancing.
items.exampleCN: 这位律师专做不动产转让业务。

items.meaning: a lawyer who prepares property transfers
items.meaningCN: 办理产权转让的律师（-er 表示人）
items.example: The conveyancer checked the title deeds.
items.exampleCN: 产权律师核对了地契。

items.meaning: a person or machine that carries things
items.meaningCN: 传送者；传送装置（-er 的变体拼写）
items.example: A conveyer carries the ore to the mill.
items.exampleCN: 传送带把矿石运到磨坊。

items.meaning: the act of carrying or communicating
items.meaningCN: 传送；传达（动名词，也是现在分词）
items.example: Conveying tone in writing is hard.
items.exampleCN: 在写作中传达语气并不容易。

items.meaning: carried or communicated
items.meaningCN: 被传送的；被传达的（-ed 构成过去分词）
items.example: The message was conveyed by hand.
items.exampleCN: 消息是手递送到的。

latinEntries.meaning: a long journey, especially by sea or in space
latinEntries.meaningCN: 航行；长途旅行（原指“上路用的给养”）

latinEntries.meaning: to turn away from the usual way
latinEntries.meaningCN: 偏离；背离（离开原来的路）

latinEntries.meaning: in the way, therefore plainly visible
latinEntries.meaningCN: 明显的（挡在路前，所以一眼看得见）

latinEntries.meaning: going before, earlier
latinEntries.meaningCN: 先前的（走在前面的）

definition_zh: 使确信；说服；证明（有罪）；使信服
definition_en: to make someone believe that something is true, or to persuade someone to do something
core_image: 把对方的怀疑按倒在地，用论据赢下这场较量
scene: 答辩幻灯片上是三组重复实验的数据曲线，评审席坐满了人。 She convinced the review panel with the data from three repeated experiments.
sceneCN: 这里 convince 是「使确信」（第 1 个义项：用证据让人相信某事为真）；句意：她用三组重复实验的数据让评审相信了结论。

derivatives.zh: 有说服力的；令人信服的

senses.title: Make someone believe a fact
senses.definition: to cause someone to believe that a statement or fact is true, using evidence or argument
senses.definitionCN: 用证据或论证使某人相信某个说法或事实为真
senses.example: The data convinced her that the method worked.
senses.exampleCN: 这些数据让她相信这个方法有效。
senses.why: Latin convincere was com- (intensive) + vincere 'to conquer'. To convince is to win completely against someone's doubt; belief is the moment doubt gives way.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 convincere 是 com-（加强）+ vincere“战胜”。convince 就是彻底赢过对方的怀疑；相信，正是怀疑让位的那一刻。

senses.title: Persuade someone to act
senses.definition: to persuade someone to do something, especially by giving reasons
senses.definitionCN: 尤指通过给出理由说服某人做某事
senses.example: He convinced his parents to let him study abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 他说服父母让他出国读书。
senses.why: Winning the argument can extend from 'believe this' to 'do this'. English allows convince + to + verb, although persuade is the older and more standard verb for action.
senses.whyCN: 赢下论证可以从“相信这件事”延伸到“去做这件事”。英语允许 convince + to + 动词，不过表示“促使行动”时，persuade 是更老也更标准的动词。

senses.title: Prove someone guilty
senses.definition: in older or legal usage, to prove that someone is guilty of a crime
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧或法律用法中，证明某人犯有某项罪行
senses.example: The evidence convinced him of theft.
senses.exampleCN: 证据证明他犯有盗窃罪。
senses.why: Latin convincere also meant 'to prove guilty'. English convict later took over that branch, leaving convince mostly for belief; the legal shadow still shows in 'convicted'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 convincere 也有“证明有罪”义。英语后来由 convict 接管这一支，convince 主要用于“使人相信”；法律阴影仍留在 convicted 里。

senses.title: Overcome an opponent in argument
senses.definition: in archaic usage, to overcome or refute an opponent in argument
senses.definitionCN: 古旧用法中，在辩论中战胜或驳倒对手
senses.example: He convinced his opponent in the public debate.
senses.exampleCN: 他在公开辩论中驳倒了对手。
senses.why: This is the plain Latin sense, 'to overcome decisively'. The modern word has softened from beating a person to beating an idea, but the contest image is the same.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语本义“彻底战胜”。现代词义已从“打败一个人”软化为“打败一个想法”，但较量意象没有变。

senses.title: Convince oneself
senses.definition: to make yourself believe something, sometimes without enough evidence
senses.definitionCN: 让自己相信某事，有时证据并不充分
senses.example: She convinced herself that the risk was small.
senses.exampleCN: 她说服自己风险很小。
senses.why: The winner and the loser are the same person: one part of the mind argues, another part gives way. The reflexive form turns the contest inward.
senses.whyCN: 赢家和输家是同一个人：心智的一部分论证，另一部分让步。反身形式把这场较量转向内部。

senses.title: Be convinced: hold a firm belief
senses.titleCN: 确信：处于坚定相信的状态
senses.definition: in the participle convinced, to be certain that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 用分词 convinced，表示确信某事为真
senses.example: I am convinced that honest records save money.
senses.exampleCN: 我确信诚实的账目能省钱。
senses.why: Once doubt has been defeated, what remains is the state of being convinced. The participle preserves the result of the contest rather than the contest itself.
senses.whyCN: 怀疑一旦被击败，留下的就是“被说服”的状态。分词保留的是较量的结果，而不是较量本身。

senses.title: Convincing: able to defeat doubt
senses.definition: in the adjective convincing, able to make someone believe something
senses.definitionCN: 形容词 convincing 表示能够让人相信某事
senses.example: Her explanation was convincing.
senses.exampleCN: 她的解释很有说服力。
senses.why: The -ing adjective names the active side: the argument carries the power to conquer doubt. The -ed adjective names the passive side: the listener has already been conquered.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形容词命名主动一方：论证带着战胜怀疑的力量。-ed 形容词命名被动一方：听者已经被战胜了。

senses.title: Usage boundary: convince vs persuade
senses.definition: convince is primarily about belief, while persuade is about belief plus action or agreement; formal writing prefers persuade for 'to do'
senses.definitionCN: convince 主要关于“相信”，persuade 则是“相信并行动/同意”；正式写作用 persuade 表示“促使去做”
senses.example: She convinced me that the plan was sound, but could not persuade me to join.
senses.exampleCN: 她让我相信这个计划是稳妥的，却没能说服我加入。
senses.why: Latin convincere is evidence-driven; persuadere is from suadere 'to advise', linked to suavis 'sweet'. Convince wins the mind, persuade wins the will as well.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 convincere 由证据驱动；persuadere 来自 suadere“劝告”，与 suavis“甜美”有关。convince 赢下的是头脑，persuade 还赢下意愿。

intro.en: Convince is a Latin word for winning. Its root vincere 'to conquer' is the same one in victory and invincible; English first used it for beating an opponent in argument, then for beating doubt. It is not convey: convey moves things along a road (via), convince wins a mind (vincere).
intro.cn: convince 是一个拉丁语的“赢”词。词根 vincere“战胜”也出现在 victory 和 invincible 里；英语先用它表示在辩论中打败对手，再表示打败怀疑。它与 convey 不同：convey 沿 via“道路”把东西送到另一端，convince 用 vincere“战胜”赢下一个头脑。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'to overcome in argument, refute'. The sense 'to persuade firmly' follows in the 1530s.
items.cn: 16 世纪 20 年代最早记录，意为“在辩论中战胜、驳倒”；“坚定地说服”义随后在 16 世纪 30 年代出现。

items.en: From Latin convincere 'to overcome decisively, refute, prove', past participle convictus.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 convincere“彻底战胜、驳倒、证明”，过去分词为 convictus。

items.en: convincere = com- (here intensive, 'completely') + vincere 'to conquer'. The prefix does not mean 'together' in this word.
items.cn: convincere = com-（此处为加强语气，“彻底”）+ vincere“战胜”。这个词里的前缀并不表示“一起”。

items.en: vincere is traced to PIE *weik- 'to fight, conquer', also the root of victor, victory and invincible. The reconstruction is generally accepted.
items.cn: vincere 被追溯到原始印欧语 *weik-“战斗、战胜”，也是 victor、victory、invincible 的词根。该重构属于一般认为是。

items.en: In law, convince once meant 'to prove guilty'. Convict took over that function, so modern English keeps the legal sense only inside convict and conviction.
items.cn: 在法律语域，convince 曾表示“证明有罪”。convict 接管了这一功能，因此现代英语只在 convict 和 conviction 里保留法律义。

items.en: Modern usage separates convince (belief) from persuade (belief plus action). Convince oneself is 18c.; the -ing/-ed pair settled into 'producing belief' and 'holding belief'.
items.cn: 现代用法把 convince（相信）与 persuade（相信并行动）分开。convince oneself 见于 18 世纪；-ing/-ed 一对固定为“产生相信”和“持有相信”。

note.en: The first group is built on the same vincere 'conquer' root or looks close to it; the second group separates proof, persuasion, reassurance and emotional pressure.
note.cn: 第一组要么同出 vincere“战胜”词根，要么词形接近；第二组区分证明、劝说、安慰和情绪施压。

entries.definition: to find someone guilty in a court. It is the legal branch that convince used to carry.
entries.definitionCN: 在法庭上判定某人有罪。它就是 convince 曾经承担的法律分支。

entries.definition: to show clearly that a quality or feeling exists. Latin evincere meant 'to prove, conquer'.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚地显示某种品质或情感存在。拉丁语 evincere 意为“证明、战胜”。

entries.definition: impossible to defeat. It contains the same vincere 'conquer'.
entries.definitionCN: 不可战胜的。它含有同一个 vincere“战胜”。

entries.definition: to make someone agree or do something by giving reasons. It aims at the will, while convince aims at belief.
entries.definitionCN: 通过给出理由使某人同意或去做。它瞄准意愿，而 convince 瞄准相信。

entries.definition: to tell someone confidently that something is true, in order to remove worry. It is about reassurance, not argument.
entries.definitionCN: 有把握地告诉某人某事为真，以消除担忧。它重在安慰，不在论证。

entries.definition: to influence someone's opinion or decision, often emotionally. It describes the pull more than the proof.
entries.definitionCN: 影响某人的观点或决定，常带情绪色彩。它描述的是拉力，而不是证据。

entries.definition: to convince someone fully by meeting the required standard of proof. It often appears as 'satisfy the court'.
entries.definitionCN: 通过达到所需证明标准而让人完全信服。常见于 satisfy the court。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: com- intensive + vincere 'conquer', with victory, invincible, convict and evince in the same family.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：com- 表加强 + vincere“战胜”，victory、invincible、convict、evince 都属同一词族。

normal.en: Vincere 'conquer' is visible in victory and invincible. Convince is a victory over doubt, not over a person.
normal.cn: vincere“战胜”在 victory 和 invincible 里看得见。convince 是对怀疑的胜利，不是对人的胜利。

normal.en: The prefix com- is intensive here: not 'together' but 'completely'. To convince is to win completely.
normal.cn: 这里的前缀 com- 表加强：不是“一起”，而是“彻底”。convince 就是彻底赢下。

normal.en: Convince somebody of something targets belief; persuade somebody to do something targets action.
normal.cn: “convince somebody of something”瞄准“相信”；“persuade somebody to do something”瞄准“行动”。

normal.en: Convict and conviction keep the old legal branch: a court conquers the presumption of innocence with proof.
normal.cn: convict 和 conviction 保留旧法律分支：法庭用证据战胜无罪推定。

normal.en: Convinced and convincing are the two ends of the same contest: the listener has been won, or the argument is winning.
normal.cn: convinced 和 convincing 是同一场较量的两端：听者已被赢下，或论证正在赢。

abstract.en: Picture a wrestler pinning doubt to the floor. The argument does not kill doubt; it holds it down until it stops moving.
abstract.cn: 想象一个摔跤手把“怀疑”按在地上。论证没有杀死怀疑，而是压住它，直到它不再动弹。

abstract.en: Belief is the silence after the struggle. The word names both the fight and the quiet that follows it.
abstract.cn: 相信是搏斗之后的安静。这个词同时命名了打斗和随后的寂静。

abstract.en: Self-persuasion is a match with only one player: the same hand both pins and is pinned.
abstract.cn: 自我说服是一场只有一个选手的比赛：同一只手既压制，也被压制。

examples.en: The video convinced the jury that the alibi was false.
examples.cn: 这段录像让陪审团相信不在场证明是假的。

examples.en: Nothing could convince him to change his mind.
examples.cn: 什么也无法说服他改变主意。

examples.en: I am convinced that the deadline can still be met.
examples.cn: 我确信这个截止日期仍然赶得上。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯温斯”——肯温斯拿着证据死磕到底，对方终于信了 → convince 使确信、说服

root: 拉丁语 com-（加强）+ vincere“战胜”，字面义“彻底战胜对方”，核心是“用证据把怀疑压下去”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of convince, all one contest: evidence wins and doubt gives way — in belief, in action, in a courtroom, in an argument, and inside oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: convince 的八个义项都是同一场较量：证据获胜、怀疑让位——发生在相信、行动、法庭、辩论以及自己内心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: evidence wrestles doubt to the ground and holds it there.
core.cn: 核心意象：证据把怀疑摔倒在地，并压住不放。

branches.en: BELIEF: the contest ends in a settled state of certainty.
branches.cn: 相信：较量以稳定的确信状态收尾。

branches.en: ACTION: winning the mind extends to winning agreement to act.
branches.cn: 行动：赢下头脑，进一步延伸为赢下行动的同意。

branches.en: PROOF AND CONTEST: the courtroom and the debate keep the original 'overcome' force.
branches.cn: 证明与较量：法庭和辩论保留了最初的“战胜”力度。

branches.en: SELF: the same struggle turns inward when you convince yourself.
branches.cn: 自我：当你说服自己时，同一场斗争转向内部。

branches.en: FORM AND BOUNDARY: -ing produces belief, -ed holds it, and persuade covers action.
branches.cn: 形式与边界：-ing 产生相信，-ed 持有相信，persuade 负责行动。

intro.en: Convince adds -ing and -ed to make the two sides of persuasion visible, and -tion for the resulting state. The Latin prefix is not productive in English here.
intro.cn: convince 加 -ing 和 -ed 显示说服的两端，加 -tion 表示结果状态。这里的拉丁前缀在英语中不是能产成分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on vincere 'to conquer': victor, victory, invincible, evince and convict all describe some kind of winning.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 vincere“战胜”上：victor、victory、invincible、evince、convict 都描述某种“赢”。

items.meaning: able to make someone believe something
items.meaningCN: 有说服力的（-ing 分词作形容词，表示主动产生效果）
items.example: She gave a convincing account of the accident.
items.exampleCN: 她对事故做了令人信服的叙述。

items.meaning: certain that something is true
items.meaningCN: 确信的（-ed 分词作形容词，表示已被说服）
items.example: He was convinced that the plan would fail.
items.exampleCN: 他确信这个计划会失败。

items.meaning: a court finding of guilt; a firmly held belief
items.meaningCN: 定罪；坚定信念（-ion 构成行为或状态名词）
items.example: Her conviction never wavered under pressure.
items.exampleCN: 在压力下，她的信念从未动摇。

items.meaning: in a way that produces belief
items.meaningCN: 令人信服地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: He argued convincingly for the new design.
items.exampleCN: 他为新设计做了有说服力的论证。

items.meaning: failing to persuade
items.meaningCN: 不能令人信服的（un- 表否定）
items.example: His excuse was unconvincing.
items.exampleCN: 他的借口难以令人信服。

items.meaning: not persuaded
items.meaningCN: 未被说服的（un- 表否定）
items.example: The board remained unconvinced.
items.exampleCN: 董事会仍然没有被说服。

items.meaning: impossible to defeat
items.meaningCN: 不可战胜的（与 vincere“战胜”同根）
items.example: The team seemed invincible that season.
items.exampleCN: 那个赛季这支队伍似乎不可战胜。

items.meaning: to show clearly; to make evident
items.meaningCN: 表明；显示（与 vincere 同根，义为“显露”）
items.example: The letter evinces real concern.
items.exampleCN: 这封信流露出真切的关切。

latinEntries.meaning: the act of winning
latinEntries.meaningCN: 胜利（战胜的结果）

latinEntries.meaning: not able to be defeated
latinEntries.meaningCN: 不可战胜的（不能被战胜）

latinEntries.meaning: to show clearly that something exists
latinEntries.meaningCN: 显示；表明（把内在的东西“赢”出来给人看）

latinEntries.meaning: to prove someone guilty; a person found guilty
latinEntries.meaningCN: 定罪；罪犯（用证据彻底战胜）

definition_zh: 合作；配合；协助；共同起作用
definition_en: to work together with someone toward a shared aim, or to do what someone asks
core_image: 两只手同时抬起同一块木板
scene: 暴雨后，一棵倒下的树横在路边，远处有救护车的声音。 After the storm the neighbours cooperated to lift the fallen tree to the side of the road so the ambulance could pass.
sceneCN: 这里 cooperate 是「合作」（第 1 个义项：为共同目标一起出力）；句意：暴雨后，邻居们合作把倒下的树抬到路边，好让救护车通过。

senses.title: Work together toward a shared aim
senses.definition: to work with other people toward a goal that all of you want
senses.definitionCN: 与其他人一起为共同想要的目标工作
senses.example: The two labs cooperated on the vaccine trial.
senses.exampleCN: 两个实验室合作开展了疫苗试验。
senses.why: cooperate is Latin com- 'with' + operari 'to work', from opus 'work'. The word literally says 'work with', so the core sense is two or more parties putting in effort at once.
senses.whyCN: cooperate 是拉丁语 com-“一起”+ operari“工作”，后者来自 opus“工作”。这个词字面就说“一起干活”，核心义是两方或多方同时出力。

senses.title: Comply with an authority
senses.definition: to do what the police, a court, or an official body asks you to do
senses.definitionCN: 按警察、法院或官方机构的要求去做
senses.example: Witnesses cooperated with the police.
senses.exampleCN: 证人配合了警方。
senses.why: One side has authority, but the verb still frames the exchange as joint activity rather than obedience. The authority needs your work to complete its own.
senses.whyCN: 一方握有权力，但这个词仍把互动框定为共同活动，而不是单纯服从。权威机构需要你的“出力”来完成它自己的工作。

senses.title: Joint action between organizations or states
senses.titleCN: 机构或国家间的联合行动
senses.definition: of organizations, governments, or states, to act jointly on a shared problem
senses.definitionCN: 机构、政府或国家就共同问题联合行动
senses.example: The border states cooperate on flood control.
senses.exampleCN: 边境各州在防洪上合作。
senses.why: The 'work with' image scales up: the workers are now institutions, and the shared task is a river, a market, or a border.
senses.whyCN: “一起干活”的意象被放大：出力者变成机构，共同任务变成一条河、一个市场或一条边境。

senses.title: Of factors: act together to produce a result
senses.definition: of conditions or forces, to combine in producing an effect
senses.definitionCN: 条件或力量共同作用，产生某种结果
senses.example: Sun, soil and rain cooperated to produce a good harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 阳光、土壤和雨水共同促成了一次丰收。
senses.why: Non-human things can also 'work with' each other. The verb personifies them briefly: each factor does its part in one joint result.
senses.whyCN: 非人的事物也可以“一起工作”。这个动词短暂地拟人化：每个因素都在同一个结果里尽了自己那份力。

senses.title: A cooperative attitude
senses.definition: in the adjective cooperative, willing to help and easy to work with
senses.definitionCN: 形容词 cooperative 表示愿意帮忙、好相处
senses.example: The staff were cooperative at every stage, and they cooperated with the audit without complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 员工在每个环节都很配合，毫无怨言地协助审计。
senses.why: Cooperation as a habit becomes a personality description. The adjective turns the act of working together into a disposition.
senses.whyCN: 把合作当成习惯，就变成对性格的描述。形容词把“一起工作”这一行为转化成一种倾向。

senses.title: A cooperative enterprise
senses.titleCN: 合作社：共同拥有的企业
senses.definition: a business owned and run jointly by the people who use it
senses.definitionCN: 由使用者共同拥有和经营的企业
senses.example: The growers cooperated to form a cooperative that buys their coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 种植户合作成立了一个收购他们咖啡的合作社。
senses.why: An institution built on the principle of working together takes the noun cooperative. Ownership itself is shared, so the economic form matches the word's image.
senses.whyCN: 按“一起干活”原则建立的组织用名词 cooperative。所有权本身就是共享的，经济形态与词的形象正好一致。

senses.title: Mutual benefit in game theory
senses.definition: in economics and game theory, to choose an action that lets both sides gain
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学与博弈论中，选择让双方都获益的行动
senses.example: Players cooperate when each gains from the other's choice.
senses.exampleCN: 当双方都能从对方的选择中获益时，玩家就会合作。
senses.why: The Latin 'work with' is formalised as a strategy: cooperation is the choice to make the joint outcome larger instead of taking a larger share of a smaller outcome.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语“一起干活”在这里被形式化为策略：合作是选择把共同结果做大，而不是去分一个更小的结果中更大的份额。

senses.title: Usage boundary: cooperation is not obedience
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：合作不等于服从
senses.definition: cooperation implies two active sides, while obedience implies one side simply carrying out orders
senses.definitionCN: 合作意味着两方都在主动出力，服从则意味着一方只是执行命令
senses.example: A witness who answers questions is cooperating; a soldier who follows orders may only be obeying.
senses.exampleCN: 回答问题的证人在合作；只执行命令的士兵可能只是服从。
senses.why: Because the root is operari 'work', cooperation needs actual contribution from both sides. Obedience comes from audire 'to hear' and needs only one side to act.
senses.whyCN: 因为词根是 operari“工作”，合作需要两方都有实际贡献。obedience 来自 audire“听”，只需要一方行动。

intro.en: Cooperate is literally 'work with': com- 'with' plus operari 'to work'. It is built on opus 'work', the same noun behind opera and office, and it is not the same word as coordinate, which is built on ordo 'order'.
intro.cn: cooperate 字面就是“一起工作”：com-“一起”加 operari“工作”。它建立在 opus“工作”上，opera、office 也来自这个词；它与 coordinate 不是同一个词，后者建立在 ordo“秩序”上。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'to act together'. The spelling co-operate is older and still used in British English.
items.cn: 16 世纪 80 年代最早记录，意为“共同行动”。带连字符的 co-operate 更老，英式英语中仍可见。

items.en: From Late Latin cooperatus, past participle of cooperari 'to work together'.
items.cn: 来自晚期拉丁语 cooperatus，即 cooperari“一起工作”的过去分词。

items.en: cooperari = com- 'with' + operari 'to work, labor', from opus 'work, task'.
items.cn: cooperari = com-“一起”+ operari“工作、劳作”，后者来自 opus“工作、任务”。

items.en: opus is traced to PIE *op- 'to work, produce in abundance'; the reconstruction is generally accepted. The same opus gives opera, operate and office (officium).
items.cn: opus 被追溯到原始印欧语 *op-“工作、丰产”，该重构属于一般认为是。同一个 opus 还给出 opera、operate 和 office（officium）。

items.en: The cooperative movement made the adjective and noun cooperative into an economic form: a store or farm owned by its members.
items.cn: 19 世纪的合作运动使形容词和名词 cooperative 成为一种经济形态：由成员共同拥有的商店或农场。

items.en: Modern English uses cooperate for shared work and compliance. The contrast with coordinate is etymological: cooperate is about doing work together, coordinate is about putting things into the same order.
items.cn: 现代英语用 cooperate 表示共同做事与配合。它与 coordinate 的对比是词源性的：cooperate 重在“一起出力”，coordinate 重在“排进同一秩序”。

note.en: The first group looks similar or shares opus 'work'; the second group separates shared work, creative partnership, one-sided help and compliance.
note.cn: 第一组词形相近或共享 opus“工作”；第二组区分共同出力、创作搭档、单方协助和遵从。

entries.definition: to work or run a machine, business, or system. Cooperation adds 'with' to the same working verb.
entries.definitionCN: 操作或运行机器、企业、系统。cooperate 在同一个“工作”动词上加上了“一起”。

entries.definition: the act of working or running something; also a medical procedure. It is the noun of operate.
entries.definitionCN: 运作；手术。它是 operate 的名词。

entries.definition: relating to a company. It looks close to cooperate but comes from corpus 'body', not opus 'work'.
entries.definitionCN: 公司的。它看起来接近 cooperate，但来自 corpus“身体”，不是 opus“工作”。

entries.definition: to work with someone, especially on a creative or intellectual project. It also has the darker sense 'to work with an enemy'.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人合作，尤指创作或学术项目。它还有“通敌”这一暗义。

entries.definition: to help someone, usually without equal responsibility for the result. Cooperation is more balanced.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助某人，通常不承担同等结果责任。cooperation 更强调对等。

entries.definition: to obey a rule, order, or request. It is one-way and rule-based, unlike cooperation.
entries.definitionCN: 遵守规则、命令或请求。它是单向、以规则为基础的，不同于合作。

entries.definition: to arrange separate parts so they fit together. Coordinate organises the pieces; cooperate supplies the joint effort.
entries.definitionCN: 安排各个部分使其配合。coordinate 整理零件，cooperate 提供共同出力。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: co- 'with' + operate 'work'. The word operate is visible inside cooperate, and opus also gives opera and office.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：co-“一起”+ operate“工作”。cooperate 里面看得见 operate，opus 还给出 opera 和 office。

normal.en: co- 'with' + operate 'work' = cooperate. If you can spell operate, you can see the whole logic of the word.
normal.cn: co-“一起”+ operate“工作”= cooperate。会拼 operate，就能看见这个词的全部逻辑。

normal.en: Opera, operate and office all come from opus 'work'; cooperate is the 'work with' branch.
normal.cn: opera、operate、office 都来自 opus“工作”；cooperate 是“与他人一起工作”这一支。

normal.en: Police ask witnesses to cooperate: they need your part of the work, not just your silence.
normal.cn: 警察请证人 cooperate：他们需要你出的那份力，而不只是你的沉默。

normal.en: A cooperative is a business where the members work together and own it together.
normal.cn: cooperative（合作社）就是成员一起干活、一起拥有的企业。

normal.en: Coordinate is the contrast word: it arranges pieces, while cooperate does the work.
normal.cn: coordinate 是对照词：它安排零件，cooperate 则出力干活。

abstract.en: Two people lift one plank: neither can hold it alone, and neither is merely obeying. That is the exact shape of cooperation.
abstract.cn: 两个人抬同一块木板：谁也无法独自拿住，谁也不是单纯服从。这正是合作的形状。

abstract.en: Think of gears that must turn together. If one gear only pretends to turn, the machine stops.
abstract.cn: 想象必须同时转动的齿轮。如果一个齿轮只是假装在转，机器就会停下。

abstract.en: Cooperation is a choice to enlarge the shared result rather than grab a bigger slice of a smaller one.
abstract.cn: 合作是选择把共同结果做大，而不是去抢一个更小结果里更大的那一块。

examples.en: The two countries agreed to cooperate on climate research.
examples.cn: 两国同意在气候研究上合作。

examples.en: The suspect refused to cooperate with the inquiry.
examples.cn: 嫌疑人拒绝配合调查。

examples.en: Several factors cooperated to make the launch a success.
examples.cn: 多个因素共同促成了这次发射成功。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阔普瑞特”——阔普瑞特和伙伴把同一块木板一起抬起来 → cooperate 合作、配合

root: 拉丁语 com-“一起”+ operari“工作”（opus“工作”），字面义“一起干活”，核心是“两方同时出力做同一件事”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of cooperate, all one act of working with: on a task, with an authority, across institutions, among factors, as an attitude, as an enterprise, as a strategy, and against the false synonym 'obey'.
sensesIntro.cn: cooperate 的八个义项都是同一个“一起出力”：在任务上、对权威、跨机构、因素之间、作为一种态度、作为一种企业、作为一种策略，以及和假同义词“服从”划清界限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two or more hands lift the same load at the same time.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只或多只手在同一时刻抬起同一份重量。

branches.en: SHARED TASK: work with a partner, or supply the part an authority needs.
branches.cn: 共同任务：与伙伴一起干，或提供权威机构需要的那份力。

branches.en: SCALE: institutions and states repeat the same hand-over-hand effort.
branches.cn: 规模：机构和国家的动作，仍是同一双手叠手的用力。

branches.en: IMPERSONAL: factors can 'work with' one another to produce a result.
branches.cn: 非人：因素之间也能“一起工作”，产生一个结果。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: a cooperative attitude becomes a co-op enterprise.
branches.cn: 制度：合作的态度固化为合作社企业。

branches.en: STRATEGY AND BOUNDARY: mutual gain by choice, and cooperation needs two active sides.
branches.cn: 策略与边界：主动选择互利，且合作必须有两方都在动。

intro.en: cooperate takes the living prefix co- and the verb operate; English then adds -ion, -ive, -ly and -ness. The root opus is not visible on the surface but holds the family together.
intro.cn: cooperate 由活的 prefix co- 加动词 operate 构成；英语再加 -ion、-ive、-ly、-ness。词根 opus 表面看不见，却把这个词族维系在一起。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on opus 'work': opera, operate, operatic and office all involve doing or producing something.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 opus“工作”上：opera、operate、operatic、office 都涉及做事或产出。

items.meaning: the act of working together
items.meaningCN: 合作；配合（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The project succeeded through close cooperation.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目靠紧密合作取得了成功。

items.meaning: willing to help; a jointly owned enterprise
items.meaningCN: 合作的；合作社（-ive 表示倾向，也可作名词）
items.example: The staff were friendly and cooperative.
items.exampleCN: 员工友好且乐于配合。

items.meaning: in a spirit of shared work
items.meaningCN: 以合作的方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The teams worked cooperatively across borders.
items.exampleCN: 各团队跨国界合作工作。

items.meaning: refusing to help or work with others
items.meaningCN: 不合作的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: An uncooperative witness slowed the case.
items.exampleCN: 一个不配合的证人拖慢了案件。

items.meaning: a person who works with others
items.meaningCN: 合作者（-or 表示施事者）
items.example: Each cooperator received a share.
items.exampleCN: 每位合作者都分到了一份。

items.meaning: the quality of being willing to work with others
items.meaningCN: 合作性（-ness 构成抽象名词）
items.example: Teachers rated the child’s cooperativeness.
items.exampleCN: 老师评估了这个孩子的合作性。

items.meaning: a cooperative shop, farm or flat
items.meaningCN: 合作社；合作公寓（cooperative 的缩略形式）
items.example: The village runs a food co-op.
items.exampleCN: 这个村子经营一家食品合作社。

items.meaning: refusal to cooperate, especially as political protest
items.meaningCN: 不合作（non- 表否定）
items.example: The movement urged noncooperation with the census.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动号召抵制人口普查。

latinEntries.meaning: a dramatic work set to music; the plural of opus
latinEntries.meaningCN: 歌剧；作品（opus 的复数，原义“作品”）

latinEntries.meaning: to work, run, or perform a function
latinEntries.meaningCN: 操作；运转（做事、发挥功能）

latinEntries.meaning: a place or role of duty and work
latinEntries.meaningCN: 办公室；职务（做事的地方与职责）

latinEntries.meaning: a work, especially a musical composition
latinEntries.meaningCN: 作品（尤指音乐作品）

definition_zh: 协调；使配合；（坐标）坐标；同等的
definition_en: to arrange different parts so that they work together smoothly; a value that locates a point; equal in rank
core_image: 把散乱的行列对齐到同一张网格上
scene: 志愿者手里拿着时刻表和对讲机。 The volunteer coordinated the departure times of the supply station, the medical point, and the shelter truck.
sceneCN: 这里 coordinate 是「协调」（第 1 个义项：安排各部分使其配合）；句意：志愿者协调了补给站、医疗点和收容车的出发时间。

pos.zh: 坐标；配套衣物（常用复数 coordinates；-ate 读 /ət/）

senses.title: Arrange parts so they work together
senses.definition: to organise different parts of an activity so that they fit together and work smoothly
senses.definitionCN: 组织一项活动的各个部分，使它们互相配合、顺利运转
senses.example: The manager coordinated the schedules of five teams.
senses.exampleCN: 经理协调了五个团队的日程。
senses.why: coordinate is Latin co- 'together' + ordinare 'to arrange', from ordo 'row, order'. The image is putting separate items into one row, so that each knows its place.
senses.whyCN: coordinate 是拉丁语 co-“一起”+ ordinare“安排”，后者来自 ordo“行列、秩序”。意象是把分开的项目排进同一行，让每一项都知道自己的位置。

senses.title: Synchronise people or agencies in time
senses.titleCN: 让人员或机构在时间上同步
senses.definition: to make people or organisations act at the right times relative to each other
senses.definitionCN: 使人员或组织相对于彼此在正确的时间行动
senses.example: Rescue teams coordinated their arrival at the site.
senses.exampleCN: 救援队协调了到达现场的时间。
senses.why: Ordering in space becomes ordering in time. The rows now line up on a timetable, so no team arrives before another is ready.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的排列变成时间上的排列。行列此时对齐在一张时刻表上，没有队伍会在另一队准备好之前到达。

senses.title: Match clothes or colours
senses.definition: to choose clothes or colours that look good together
senses.definitionCN: 选择放在一起好看的衣物或颜色
senses.example: She coordinated a blue jacket with grey trousers.
senses.exampleCN: 她用蓝色外套搭配灰色长裤。
senses.why: Separate garments are arranged into one visual order. The same 'line them up' act is applied to colour and cut rather than to schedules.
senses.whyCN: 分开的衣物被排进同一个视觉秩序。同一个“排整齐”的动作，此时用在颜色和剪裁上，而不是日程上。

senses.title: Mathematics: a pair of coordinates
senses.definition: one of a set of numbers that together locate a point on a line, plane, or in space
senses.definitionCN: 一组数字中的一个，与其余数字共同确定点在线、平面或空间中的位置
senses.example: The point has coordinates (3, 5).
senses.exampleCN: 这个点的坐标是 (3, 5)。
senses.why: A coordinate is a number that says where a point sits in an ordered grid. The medieval sense 'of the same order' becomes a numerical address.
senses.whyCN: 坐标就是一个数字，说明点在有序网格里的位置。中世纪“同一秩序”的含义，在这里变成了数字化的地址。

senses.title: Geographic coordinates
senses.definition: latitude and longitude values that fix a place on the Earth's surface
senses.definitionCN: 确定地球表面某地位置的纬度和经度数值
senses.example: The ship sent its coordinates before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 船在暴风雨前发出了自己的坐标。
senses.why: The Earth's grid is the same ordering device at global scale. Two numbers put a place into a row and column that everyone can read.
senses.whyCN: 地球网格是同一套排序装置在全球尺度上的版本。两个数字把一个地点放进人人都能读懂的“行与列”。

senses.title: Equal in rank or status
senses.definition: in the adjective coordinate, having the same rank or importance as another part
senses.definitionCN: 形容词 coordinate 表示与另一部分级别或重要性相同
senses.example: The two agencies are coordinate branches of the government.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个机构是政府的同级分支。
senses.why: Medieval Latin coordinatus literally meant 'of the same order'. Equal rank is the static version of the same row image: neither part sits above the other.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪拉丁语 coordinatus 字面就是“同一秩序的”。同级就是同一行意象的静态版本：没有任何一部分坐在另一部分之上。

senses.title: Grammar: coordinate clauses
senses.definition: in grammar, coordinate clauses or conjunctions are of equal grammatical rank and are joined without one depending on the other
senses.definitionCN: 语法中，并列从句或并列连词地位相同，连接时一方不依赖另一方
senses.example: The conjunction 'and' joins two coordinate clauses.
senses.exampleCN: 连词 and 连接两个并列从句。
senses.why: Grammar borrows the rank sense: clauses of the same order stand side by side, joined by and, but, or or so, with no main-subordinate relation.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了“同级”含义：同一秩序的分句并排站立，用 and、but、or、so 连接，没有主从关系。

senses.title: Coordinate with someone
senses.definition: to communicate with another person or group so that your plans do not conflict
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人或团体沟通，使双方计划不冲突
senses.example: Coordinate with the venue before booking speakers.
senses.exampleCN: 订演讲者之前先和场地方对接。
senses.why: The reciprocal verb sense: each side orders its own actions against the other's timetable. The verb is now about exchange and alignment, not one-way command.
senses.whyCN: 这是相互动词义：每一方都按对方的时间表调整自己的行动。动词此时关于交流与对齐，而不是单向命令。

senses.title: Coordination: the resulting order
senses.definition: in the noun coordination, the state or skill of parts working together smoothly
senses.definitionCN: 名词 coordination 表示各部分顺利配合的状态或能力
senses.example: The operation required precise coordination, and the teams coordinated without a single gap.
senses.exampleCN: 这次行动需要精确的协调，而各团队配合得毫无缝隙。
senses.why: The noun names the finished order rather than the act of arranging. What began as rows being lined up ends as a system that runs without friction.
senses.whyCN: 名词命名的是排好之后的秩序，而不是排列动作本身。最初是把行列对齐，最后得到一个无摩擦运转的系统。

intro.en: Coordinate is an 'order' word: co- 'together' + ordo 'row, rank'. It is often confused with cooperate, but cooperate is built on opus 'work'. Coordinate arranges the pieces; cooperate supplies the joint effort.
intro.cn: coordinate 是一个“秩序”词：co-“一起”+ ordo“行列、等级”。它常与 cooperate 混淆，但 cooperate 建立在 opus“工作”上。coordinate 把零件排好，cooperate 提供共同出力。

items.en: First recorded as an adjective meaning 'of the same order or rank'. The verb 'to place in the same order' appears in the 1660s.
items.cn: 17 世纪 40 年代最早记录为形容词，意为“同一秩序或等级的”；动词“排进同一秩序”见于 17 世纪 60 年代。

items.en: From Medieval Latin coordinatus, past participle of coordinare 'to set in order, arrange'.
items.cn: 来自中世纪拉丁语 coordinatus，即 coordinare“排列、安排”的过去分词。

items.en: coordinare = co- 'with, together' + ordinare 'to arrange', from ordo (genitive ordinis) 'row, rank, series, arrangement'.
items.cn: coordinare = co-“一起”+ ordinare“安排”，后者来自 ordo（属格 ordinis）“行列、等级、系列、安排”。

items.en: ordo is traced to PIE *ar- 'to fit together', also behind art, arm and order. The link is generally accepted rather than certain.
items.cn: ordo 被追溯到原始印欧语 *ar-“拼合在一起”，art、arm、order 也出自这里。这一联系属于一般认为是，而非确证。

items.en: Mathematics adopted coordinates for points on a grid after Descartes (1637); geography extended them to latitude and longitude. Grammar added coordinate clauses in the 19c.
items.cn: 笛卡尔（1637）之后，数学用 coordinates 表示网格上的点；地理学把它扩展到经纬度；语法在 19 世纪加入 coordinate clause。

items.en: Modern English uses coordinate for management, schedules, design and data. The noun coordinates (clothes, map positions) keeps the plural because a point needs more than one number.
items.cn: 现代英语用 coordinate 表示管理、日程、设计与数据。名词复数 coordinates（配套衣物、地图位置）保留复数，因为确定一个点需要不止一个数字。

note.en: The first group shares ordo 'order' or the co- shape; the second group separates arrangement, timing, harmony and physical alignment.
note.cn: 第一组共享 ordo“秩序”或 co- 词形；第二组区分安排、对时、和谐与实体对齐。

entries.definition: in mathematics, the vertical value of a coordinate pair; literally 'ordered'.
entries.definitionCN: 数学中坐标对的纵坐标；字面义“被排列的”。

entries.definition: lower in rank. It is the opposite of coordinate in the 'equal rank' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 级别较低的。在“同级”义上，它是 coordinate 的反面。

entries.definition: to work together. It shares co- but comes from opus 'work', not ordo 'order'.
entries.definitionCN: 合作。它同样有 co-，但来自 opus“工作”，不是 ordo“秩序”。

entries.definition: to arrange people or things into a working structure. It is broader and more one-directional than coordinate.
entries.definitionCN: 把人或物安排成可运转的结构。它比 coordinate 更宽泛，也更单向。

entries.definition: to make events happen at the same time or rate. It focuses on timing rather than overall order.
entries.definitionCN: 使事件在同一时间或同一速率发生。它聚焦时间，而不是整体秩序。

entries.definition: to make parts combine in a pleasing or conflict-free way. It stresses smoothness, not rank.
entries.definitionCN: 使各部分以悦目或无冲突的方式结合。它强调顺畅，不强调等级。

entries.definition: to bring things into a straight line or into agreement. It is the physical version of coordinate.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物排成直线或使之一致。它是 coordinate 的实体版本。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: co- 'together' + ordo 'row, order'. The word order is hidden in the Latin root, and coordinates on a map show the same grid.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：co-“一起”+ ordo“行列、秩序”。order 藏在拉丁词根里，地图上的 coordinates 展示同一张网格。

normal.en: co- 'together' + ordinate 'arrange' = arrange together. The family of order, ordinary and subordinate shares the same ordo.
normal.cn: co-“一起”+ ordinate“安排”=一起排好。order、ordinary、subordinate 都共享同一个 ordo。

normal.en: Coordinates on a map are two numbers that place you in a row and a column: order made numerical.
normal.cn: 地图上的 coordinates 是两个数字，把你放进一行一列：秩序变成了数字。

normal.en: A coordinate clause has the same rank as its neighbour; a subordinate clause does not. Rank is the grammar version of the row.
normal.cn: coordinate clause 与相邻分句同级；subordinate clause 则不是。等级就是“行列”的语法版本。

normal.en: Coordinate with the venue means line your timetable against theirs, not send them orders.
normal.cn: “coordinate with the venue”意思是把自己的时间表与对方对齐，而不是给对方下命令。

normal.en: Remember the contrast: coordinate uses ordo 'order'; cooperate uses opus 'work'.
normal.cn: 记住对比：coordinate 用 ordo“秩序”；cooperate 用 opus“工作”。

abstract.en: Imagine a messy shelf being sorted into one straight row. Nothing new is made; the parts simply find their places.
abstract.cn: 想象一个乱架子被整理成一条直线。没有制造新东西，只是每个部分找到了自己的位置。

abstract.en: A conductor does not play any instrument; the conductor only makes the players share one beat. Coordination is that shared beat.
abstract.cn: 指挥不演奏任何乐器；指挥只让演奏者共享同一个拍子。协调就是那个共享的拍子。

abstract.en: Two clocks set to the same time do not become one clock. They remain two, but their hands move together.
abstract.cn: 两只调成同一时间的钟不会变成一只钟。它们仍是两只，只是指针一起走。

examples.en: We need to coordinate our arrival times so no one waits alone.
examples.cn: 我们需要协调到达时间，别让任何人独自等待。

examples.en: The rescue effort was coordinated from a single command centre.
examples.cn: 救援行动由一个指挥中心统一协调。

examples.en: The GPS device shows the hiker's exact coordinates.
examples.cn: GPS 设备显示徒步者的精确坐标。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阔迪内特”——阔迪内特把五支队伍的时刻表对齐成同一张表 → coordinate 协调、使配合

root: 拉丁语 co-“共同”+ ordo/ordinare“行列、安排”，字面义“排进同一行列”，核心是“让各部分对齐、按同一秩序运转”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of coordinate, all one act of lining things up: schedules, teams, clothes, numbers on a grid, places on a map, equal ranks, grammar, communication, and the finished order itself.
sensesIntro.cn: coordinate 的九个义项都是同一个“对齐”动作：日程、团队、衣物、网格数字、地图位置、同级身份、语法、沟通，以及最终形成的秩序本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered rows are pulled into one aligned grid.
core.cn: 核心意象：散乱的行列被拉进同一张对齐的网格。

branches.en: ORDERING: parts and people are arranged so their actions fit.
branches.cn: 排序：零件与人被安排得彼此配合。

branches.en: VISUAL: clothes and colours are matched into one look.
branches.cn: 视觉：衣物与颜色被搭配成同一个外观。

branches.en: GRID: numbers and latitude-longitude place a point in an ordered system.
branches.cn: 网格：数字与经纬度把点放进有序系统。

branches.en: RANK: equal status in government or grammar is the same row made abstract.
branches.cn: 等级：政府或语法中的同等地位，是同一条行列的抽象版本。

branches.en: RECIPROCAL: coordination is two-way alignment and the order that results.
branches.cn: 相互：协调是双向对齐，以及由此形成的秩序。

intro.en: coordinate takes co- and the Latin verb ordinare; English adds -ion for the process and -or for the person. The root ordo also appears in order, ordinary and subordinate.
intro.cn: coordinate 由 co- 加拉丁动词 ordinare 构成；英语加 -ion 表示过程，加 -or 表示人。词根 ordo 还出现在 order、ordinary、subordinate 里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on ordo 'row, rank, order': order, ordinary, subordinate, inordinate and ordain all arrange things by rank or sequence.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 ordo“行列、等级、秩序”上：order、ordinary、subordinate、inordinate、ordain 都按等级或顺序安排事物。

items.meaning: the act or state of parts working together
items.meaningCN: 协调；配合（-ion 构成行为或状态名词）
items.example: Good coordination kept the event on schedule.
items.exampleCN: 良好的协调让活动按计划进行。

items.meaning: a person who organises people and activities
items.meaningCN: 协调者；统筹人（-or 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The volunteer coordinator assigned every task.
items.exampleCN: 志愿者协调人分配了所有任务。

items.meaning: working together smoothly; matched in style
items.meaningCN: 协调一致的；搭配得体的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The response was fast and well coordinated.
items.exampleCN: 应对迅速且协调良好。

items.meaning: badly organised, or moving awkwardly
items.meaningCN: 缺乏协调的；动作笨拙的（un- 表示否定）
items.example: Uncoordinated efforts wasted time and money.
items.exampleCN: 缺乏协调的努力浪费了时间和金钱。

items.meaning: the act of bringing parts into order
items.meaningCN: 协调（动名词，也是现在分词）
items.example: Coordinating the two teams took weeks.
items.exampleCN: 协调两个团队花了好几周。

items.meaning: serving to bring things into order
items.meaningCN: 协调性的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The role is purely coordinative.
items.exampleCN: 这个角色纯属协调性质。

items.meaning: the numbers that fix a position
items.meaningCN: 坐标（-s 构成复数名词）
items.example: The pilot read the coordinates aloud.
items.exampleCN: 飞行员大声念出坐标。

items.structure: Latin ordinare (set in order) — same root as coordinate
items.meaning: the vertical axis value in a graph
items.meaningCN: 纵坐标（同出拉丁语 ordinare“排列”）
items.example: Plot the ordinate against the abscissa.
items.exampleCN: 把纵坐标对横坐标作图。

latinEntries.meaning: arrangement, sequence, or a command
latinEntries.meaningCN: 顺序；秩序；命令（按行列排好）

latinEntries.meaning: normal, usual, not special
latinEntries.meaningCN: 普通的；平常的（处在通常秩序中）

latinEntries.meaning: lower in rank; to place under another
latinEntries.meaningCN: 下级的；使从属（被排在下面）

latinEntries.meaning: excessive, beyond proper order
latinEntries.meaningCN: 过度的；无节制的（超出应有秩序）

definition_zh: 核心；果心；地核；（事务的）要点；核心肌肉
definition_en: the central or most important part of something, such as a fruit, a planet, a problem, or a body
core_image: 果实正中最紧的那团种子
scene: 砧板上放着一个切开的苹果和一把小刀。 She cut the apple open, removed the core in the middle, and said that part was too hard and sour to eat.
sceneCN: 这里 core 是「果心」（第 1 个义项：水果正中的种子部分）；句意：她切开苹果，把中间的果心挖掉，说这部分又硬又酸不能吃。

pos.zh: 核心；果心；地核；（处理器）核心

senses.title: The central part of a fruit
senses.definition: the hard central part of an apple, pear, or similar fruit, containing the seeds
senses.definitionCN: 苹果、梨等水果正中较硬、含种子的部分
senses.example: Cut out the apple core before juicing.
senses.exampleCN: 榨汁前先把苹果核去掉。
senses.why: The oldest recorded sense is 'heart or inmost part', and fruit is where the image is easiest to see. The word's origin is source uncertain, but the common hypothesis links it to Latin cor 'heart'.
senses.whyCN: 最早记录的义项是“心脏或最里面的部分”，而水果最容易看见这个画面。这个词的来源不确定，但常见假说把它与拉丁语 cor“心”联系起来。

senses.title: The central part of the Earth
senses.definition: the dense central region of the Earth or another planet, below the mantle
senses.definitionCN: 地球或其他行星位于地幔之下的致密中心区域
senses.example: Iron flows in the Earth's outer core.
senses.exampleCN: 铁在地球的外核中流动。
senses.why: The 'heart' of the body becomes the heart of the planet. The central position, not the material, is what the word names.
senses.whyCN: 身体的“心脏”变成行星的心脏。这个词命名的是中心位置，而不是具体材料。

senses.title: The most important part of an issue
senses.titleCN: 要点：问题最要紧的部分
senses.definition: the central and most important part of an idea, argument, or problem
senses.definitionCN: 观念、论证或问题中最中心、最重要的部分
senses.example: Trust is at the core of the partnership.
senses.exampleCN: 信任是这段合作关系的核心。
senses.why: The heart metaphor moves from space to meaning: what sits at the centre holds the rest together. Remove it, and the argument falls apart.
senses.whyCN: 心脏比喻从空间移到意义：位于中心的东西支撑着其余部分。拿掉它，整个论证就散了。

senses.title: The essential group within a larger group
senses.titleCN: 核心骨干：群体中最要紧的一小群
senses.definition: a small group of committed people who keep a larger organisation or movement going
senses.definitionCN: 维持较大组织或运动运转的一小群坚定成员
senses.example: A core of ten volunteers ran the shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 十名志愿者的核心团队撑起了收容站。
senses.why: Here the heart is made of people. The core is the part that pumps, while the rest of the group comes and goes around it.
senses.whyCN: 这里的心脏由人组成。核心是“泵血”的那部分，其余成员围绕它来来去去。

senses.title: Adjective: central and essential
senses.titleCN: 形容词：核心的、必不可少的
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean basic, central, and not optional
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示基础的、中心的、不可省略的
senses.example: Reading is a core skill in every subject.
senses.exampleCN: 阅读是每门学科的核心技能。
senses.why: The noun's centre image becomes an attributive label. A core skill is one the rest of the structure is built around.
senses.whyCN: 名词的中心意象变成了定语标签。核心技能就是其余结构围着它搭建的那一项。

senses.title: Physics: a reactor core
senses.definition: the central part of a nuclear reactor where the fission reaction takes place
senses.definitionCN: 核反应堆中进行裂变反应的中央部分
senses.example: The reactor core must be cooled continuously.
senses.exampleCN: 反应堆堆芯必须持续冷却。
senses.why: The technical sense keeps the literal centre: the reaction happens in the middle, and everything else is shielding, cooling, or control.
senses.whyCN: 技术义保留字面上的中心：反应发生在正中，其余部分都是屏蔽、冷却或控制。

senses.title: Computing: a processor core
senses.definition: an independent processing unit inside a CPU, able to run instructions on its own
senses.definitionCN: 中央处理器内部能独立执行指令的处理单元
senses.example: A quad-core chip runs four tasks at once.
senses.exampleCN: 四核芯片可以同时运行四项任务。
senses.why: A chip contains several 'hearts', each doing its own work. Multi-core is the same image applied to silicon.
senses.whyCN: 一块芯片里装着好几个“心脏”，各自干活。多核就是把同一意象用到硅片上。

senses.title: Anatomy and fitness: the body's core
senses.definition: the muscles of the trunk, especially those that stabilise the spine and pelvis
senses.definitionCN: 躯干肌肉，尤其是稳定脊柱和骨盆的肌肉
senses.example: Planks strengthen the core and protect the lower back.
senses.exampleCN: 平板支撑能强化核心、保护下背。
senses.why: The trunk is the body's centre, and the muscles there hold everything else upright. The word returns to the body from which it started.
senses.whyCN: 躯干是身体的中点，那里的肌肉把其余部分撑直。这个词又回到了它出发的地方——身体。

senses.title: To the core: completely
senses.definition: in the phrase to the core, completely and in every part
senses.definitionCN: 短语 to the core 表示彻底地、每一部分都如此
senses.example: He was shaken to the core by the verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 判决让他彻底震动了。
senses.why: If something reaches the core, it has gone past the surface and into the centre. The spatial image becomes an intensifier.
senses.whyCN: 如果某件事到达 core，它就穿过了表面、进到了中心。空间意象由此变成了强调词。

intro.en: Core is an old word whose origin is not settled. The common hypothesis is Latin cor 'heart' through Old French, but the dictionaries mark it as uncertain, so the deep link should not be presented as fact.
intro.cn: core 是一个来源未定的老词。常见假说认为它经古法语来自拉丁语 cor“心”，但词典把它标为不确定，因此最深层联系不能当作事实来讲。

items.en: First recorded meaning 'heart or inmost part of the body', and soon applied to the centre of fruit. The origin of the English word is source uncertain.
items.cn: 最早记录于 14 世纪晚期，意为“心脏或身体最里面的部分”，很快也用于水果中心。这个英语词的来源不确定。

items.en: Perhaps from Old French cor 'core, heart' (12c.), from Latin cor 'heart' (genitive cordis). This route is generally accepted, not established.
items.cn: 可能来自古法语 cor（12 世纪）“果心、心”，再上溯拉丁语 cor“心”（属格 cordis）。这条路径属于一般认为是，并非确证。

items.en: Latin cor is from PIE *kerd- 'heart', the same root as cardiac, courage, concord and record. The PIE reconstruction is standard; the English borrowing remains source uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cor 来自原始印欧语 *kerd-“心”，与 cardiac、courage、concord、record 同根。原始印欧语重构是通行的，但英语借入这一环仍来源不确定。

items.en: The sense 'central part of a fruit' is recorded in the 15c.; the general sense 'central or vital part of anything' follows from it.
items.cn: “水果中心部分”义见于 15 世纪；“任何事物中心或要害部分”的一般义由此发展而来。

items.en: Nuclear reactor core (1940s), magnetic core memory (1950s) and multi-core processors (2000s) extend the centre image into technology.
items.cn: 核反应堆堆芯（20 世纪 40 年代）、磁芯存储器（50 年代）和多核处理器（2000 年代）把中心意象扩展到技术领域。

items.en: Core values, core curriculum, core muscles and to the core show the word working as an adjective and as an idiom of intensity.
items.cn: core values、core curriculum、core muscles、to the core 显示这个词既能作定语，也能构成表示“彻底”的习语。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds close but belongs to 'body' words; the second group is about central position or the edible centre.
note.cn: 第一组词形或读音接近，却属于“身体”词；第二组才表示中心位置或可食用的正中部分。

entries.definition: a body of troops or a group of people with one role. It comes from Latin corpus 'body', not cor 'heart'.
entries.definitionCN: 军团，或承担同一职能的一群人。它来自拉丁语 corpus“身体”，不是 cor“心”。

entries.definition: a dead body. It is from Latin corpus 'body' and has nothing to do with a fruit core.
entries.definitionCN: 尸体。它来自拉丁语 corpus“身体”，与果心毫无关系。

entries.definition: a thin rope or a wire. It comes from Greek khorde 'string', not from cor 'heart'.
entries.definitionCN: 细绳或电线。它来自希腊语 khorde“弦”，不是 cor“心”。

entries.definition: the organ that pumps blood; also the emotional or central part. It is the literal source of the core metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 泵血的器官；也指情感或中心部分。它是 core 比喻的字面来源。

entries.definition: the central part of an atom, a cell, or a group. It stresses the thing at the centre rather than its importance.
entries.definitionCN: 原子、细胞或群体的中心部分。它强调位于中心的那个东西，而不强调其重要性。

entries.definition: the softer part inside a nut or seed, or the essential part of an idea. It is closer to the fruit sense than to the general sense.
entries.definitionCN: 坚果或种子内部较软的部分，或观念的核心。它比一般义更接近“果实中心”义。

entries.definition: the middle point of something. It is purely spatial, while core adds importance.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的中点。它纯指空间，而 core 还带有“重要”意味。

normalIntro.en: Real relatives: cor/cordis 'heart' gives cardiac, cordial, courage, concord and record. The English core itself may or may not come from that family.
normalIntro.cn: 真实同族词：cor/cordis“心”给出 cardiac、cordial、courage、concord、record。英语 core 本身是否来自这一族，仍不确定。

normal.en: An apple core is the part at the exact centre; cut the apple across and the core is what the two halves share.
normal.cn: 苹果的 core 就在正中心；横着切开，core 是两半共同拥有的那一块。

normal.en: The Earth's core, a reactor core and a chip core all sit in the middle and do the main work.
normal.cn: 地核、反应堆堆芯、芯片核心都位于正中，并承担主要工作。

normal.en: Core values are the beliefs everything else is built around, just as the core holds the fruit together.
normal.cn: 核心价值观就是其余一切围着它搭建的信念，正如 core 把果实撑在一起。

normal.en: To the core means all the way in: not surface damage, but damage at the centre.
normal.cn: to the core 表示一直伤到最里面：不是表面受损，而是中心受损。

normal.en: Core muscles stabilise the trunk, the body's own middle.
normal.cn: 核心肌肉稳定躯干，也就是身体自己的中部。

abstract.en: Picture a fruit cut in half: the seeds sit in one tight cluster at the centre, and every edible part arranges itself around that cluster.
abstract.cn: 想象一个切成两半的果实：种子紧紧聚在正中，所有可食部分都围着这团种子排列。

abstract.en: The centre is not always the biggest part. It is the part that, if removed, makes the whole structure lose its shape.
abstract.cn: 中心未必是最大的部分，而是那个一旦拿掉、整个结构就散形的部分。

abstract.en: A heart is hidden behind ribs and muscle, yet it is the reason the visible body keeps moving.
abstract.cn: 心脏藏在肋骨和肌肉后面，却是可见的身体能持续运动的理由。

examples.en: The core of the argument is that prevention is cheaper than repair.
examples.cn: 这个论证的核心是：预防比修补更便宜。

examples.en: The company treats customer trust as a core value.
examples.cn: 这家公司把客户信任视为核心价值观。

examples.en: The drill brought up a core of ice from two kilometres down.
examples.cn: 钻机从两公里深处取出一段冰芯。

dict_mnemonic.text: “考儿”——考儿专挑苹果正中间那块挖出来 → core 果心、核心

root: 词源存疑，一般认为是拉丁语 cor“心”（属格 cordis），核心是“最里面、最要紧的那一团”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of core, all one centre: the seed cluster in fruit, the middle of the planet, the heart of an argument, the committed group, the essential adjective, a reactor, a chip, the trunk, and the innermost self.
sensesIntro.cn: core 的九个义项都是同一个“中心”：果实里的种子团、行星正中、论证要害、坚定的核心成员、作定语的“核心”、反应堆堆芯、芯片核心、躯干，以及最内在的自我。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the tight cluster at the exact middle that holds the rest in shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：位于正中的那团紧实结构，把其余部分撑住。

branches.en: FRUIT: the literal centre, with seeds inside.
branches.cn: 果实：字面上的中心，里面包着种子。

branches.en: GEOLOGY: the same centre at planetary scale.
branches.cn: 地质：同一中心放大到行星尺度。

branches.en: ESSENCE: the centre of an argument, the essential adjective, and the idiom 'to the core'.
branches.cn: 本质：论证的中心、作定语的“核心”，以及 to the core 这一习语。

branches.en: LIVING CENTRE: a committed group, or the trunk muscles that hold the body upright.
branches.cn: 活的核心：坚定的核心成员，或撑直身体的核心肌肉。

branches.en: TECHNICAL: reactor and processor cores keep the literal middle.
branches.cn: 技术：反应堆堆芯与处理器核心保留字面意义上的正中。

intro.en: Core is a free morpheme, so English mostly compounds it (core values, multi-core) or adds -er and -less. The Latin heart family is a separate set of words.
intro.cn: core 是自由语素，英语主要用它构成复合词（core values、multi-core），或加 -er、-less。拉丁语“心”词族则是另一组词。

latinIntro.en: If the Latin hypothesis is right, the family is cor/cordis 'heart': cordial, cardiac, concord, record and courage all carry that centre-of-the-body image.
latinIntro.cn: 如果拉丁语假说成立，这一族就是 cor/cordis“心”：cordial、cardiac、concord、record、courage 都带着“身体中心”的意象。

items.meaning: a tool that removes the core of fruit
items.meaningCN: 去果核器（-er 表示做该动作的工具）
items.example: An apple corer makes the job quick.
items.exampleCN: 苹果去核器让这件事很快。

items.meaning: the act of removing a core, or taking a cylindrical sample
items.meaningCN: 去核；取芯（-ing 构成活动名词）
items.example: Ice coring gives climate records.
items.exampleCN: 冰芯取样提供气候记录。

items.meaning: having no core
items.meaningCN: 无芯的（-less 表示没有）
items.example: The coreless design saves weight.
items.exampleCN: 无芯设计减轻了重量。

items.meaning: the most committed members of a group; also intense or explicit
items.meaningCN: 核心骨干；硬核的（hard 与 core 的复合词）
items.example: Only the hardcore fans stayed to the end.
items.exampleCN: 只有铁杆粉丝留到了最后。

items.meaning: having several processing cores
items.meaningCN: 多核的（multi- 表多，复合词）
items.example: The lab bought a multicore server.
items.exampleCN: 实验室买了一台多核服务器。

items.meaning: mild in content; not explicit
items.meaningCN: 软性的；内容不露骨的（soft + core 复合词）
items.example: The magazine ran a softcore version of the story.
items.exampleCN: 这本杂志刊登了这个故事的温和版本。

items.meaning: having the central part removed, or fitted with a core
items.meaningCN: 去核的；带芯的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: Add the cored apples to the pan.
items.exampleCN: 把去过核的苹果放进锅里。

items.meaning: a cylindrical sample drilled out of rock, ice or sediment
items.meaningCN: 岩心样品；钻取样本（复合名词）
items.example: The drill brought up a core sample from the ice.
items.exampleCN: 钻机从冰层中取出一份岩心样品。

latinEntries.meaning: friendly and warm; originally 'of the heart'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 热情友好的（原义“发自内心”）

latinEntries.meaning: relating to the heart
latinEntries.meaningCN: 心脏的（希腊语 kardia 与拉丁 cor 同源）

latinEntries.meaning: agreement, hearts together
latinEntries.meaningCN: 和睦；一致（心在一起）

latinEntries.meaning: to remember, to commit to the heart; a written account
latinEntries.meaningCN: 记录（原义“记在心里”）

definition_zh: 公司的；法人的；团体的；共同组成的
definition_en: relating to a corporation or a large business, or shared by all members of a group
core_image: 许多人被铸成同一个法人身体
scene: 新员工在宣传片里看到同一栋大楼、同一句口号。 In the new recruitment film the staff saw the same tower, the same slogan, and the same corporate logo.
sceneCN: 这里 corporate 是「公司的」（第 1 个义项：与公司有关的）；句意：在新宣传片里，员工看到同一栋大楼、同一句口号和同一个公司标志。

derivatives.zh: 社团主义的；社团主义者

senses.title: Relating to a business corporation
senses.definition: connected with a corporation or a large company rather than an individual
senses.definitionCN: 与公司或大企业有关，而不是与个人有关
senses.example: The company moved its corporate headquarters downtown.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把总部搬到了市中心。
senses.why: corporate is Latin corpus 'body' + -ate. A corporation is a group legally treated as one body, so corporate describes whatever belongs to that body.
senses.whyCN: corporate 是拉丁语 corpus“身体”+ -ate。corporation 是被法律当作一个身体看待的群体，因此 corporate 描述属于这个身体的一切。

senses.title: Of large companies as a social force
senses.titleCN: 作为社会力量的大企业
senses.definition: relating to big business as a political, cultural, or economic power
senses.definitionCN: 与作为政治、文化或经济力量的大企业有关
senses.example: The film criticises corporate power.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片批评企业权力。
senses.why: When a legal body grows large, it acts almost like a person with interests. Corporate then names the collective actor, not just its paperwork.
senses.whyCN: 当一个法律身体变大，它几乎像一个有利益的人那样行动。corporate 此时命名的是集体行动者，而不只是它的文件。

senses.title: Shared by a group
senses.definition: belonging to or shared by all members of a group
senses.definitionCN: 属于或由群体全体成员共同拥有
senses.example: The report is a corporate effort, not one person's work.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是集体努力的结果，不是一个人的工作。
senses.why: The 'one body' image makes authorship collective. A corporate effort comes from the body as a whole, even if many hands made it.
senses.whyCN: “一个身体”的意象使作者身份变成集体的。集体努力来自整个身体，即使有许多只手参与。

senses.title: United in one legal body
senses.definition: in legal and historical usage, formed into a single body with legal personality
senses.definitionCN: 在法律与历史用法中，组成具有法人人格的单一团体
senses.example: The bishops met as a corporate body.
senses.exampleCN: 主教们以一个法人团体的身份开会。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: a group is 'bodied' into one entity that can hold property and act in law. The body is not physical but legal.
senses.whyCN: 这是最老的义项：一群人被“结成身体”，成为一个能持有财产、在法律上行动的实体。这个身体不是物理的，而是法律的。

senses.title: Of corporate law, finance, and governance
senses.titleCN: 公司法、金融与治理层面的
senses.definition: relating to the legal and financial structure of companies, such as boards, shares, and mergers
senses.definitionCN: 与公司的法律和财务结构有关，如董事会、股份和并购
senses.example: Corporate law governs mergers and acquisitions.
senses.exampleCN: 公司法规范并购活动。
senses.why: A legal body needs organs and rules: a board, shareholders, meetings. Corporate marks the level at which the body itself, not its employees, is the subject.
senses.whyCN: 法律身体需要器官和规则：董事会、股东、会议。corporate 标记的是“身体本身”而非员工作为行为主体的层级。

senses.title: Corporate identity and branding
senses.definition: relating to the visual and verbal identity a company presents to the public
senses.definitionCN: 与公司向公众呈现的视觉和语言识别系统有关
senses.example: They redesigned the corporate logo and colours.
senses.exampleCN: 他们重新设计了公司标志和配色。
senses.why: A body needs a face. The logo, typeface and slogan give the collective body one recognisable appearance.
senses.whyCN: 身体需要一张脸。标志、字体和口号给这个集体身体一个可辨认的外观。

senses.title: Of a municipality or other incorporated body
senses.definition: relating to any group given legal personality, such as a city or a charity
senses.definitionCN: 与任何被赋予法人资格的群体有关，如城市或慈善机构
senses.example: The city is a corporate entity with its own powers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市是一个拥有自身权力的法人实体。
senses.why: Incorporation is not limited to business. A city, university or charity can also be one body in law, and corporate describes that status.
senses.whyCN: 法人化并不限于商业。城市、大学或慈善机构也可以在法律上成为一个身体，corporate 描述的就是这种身份。

senses.title: Derived family: corporation and corporatism
senses.definition: in corporation and corporatism, the 'body' image is applied to a company or to a state organised by occupational groups
senses.definitionCN: 在 corporation 与 corporatism 中，“身体”意象被用于公司，或被用于按职业团体组织起来的国家
senses.example: Corporatism builds an economy out of corporate bodies such as guilds and employers' groups.
senses.exampleCN: 社团主义用行会、雇主团体这类法人团体来搭建经济。
senses.why: The same body image produces very different institutions: a company, a city, or a state built from occupational corporations. The suffix changes, the body stays.
senses.whyCN: 同一个身体意象产生很不同的制度：公司、城市，或由职业团体构成的国家。后缀变了，身体还在。

intro.en: Corporate comes from corpus 'body'. A corporation is a group made into one legal body, and corporate describes anything belonging to that body — business, city, or state.
intro.cn: corporate 来自 corpus“身体”。corporation 是被制成一个法律身体的群体，corporate 描述属于这个身体的一切——企业、城市或国家。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'united in one body'. The commercial sense 'of a business corporation' develops later.
items.cn: 15 世纪最早记录，意为“结成一体”。“属于商业公司”的义项后来才发展出来。

items.en: From Latin corporatus, past participle of corporare 'to form into a body', from corpus 'body'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 corporatus，即 corporare“使成为身体”的过去分词，后者来自 corpus“身体”。

items.en: corpus (genitive corporis) 'body' is traced to PIE *kwrep- 'body, form, appearance'; the reconstruction is generally accepted.
items.cn: corpus（属格 corporis）“身体”被追溯到原始印欧语 *kwrep-“身体、形体、外观”；该重构属于一般认为是。

items.en: The adjective corporate attaches to corporations and incorporated bodies. In the 19c. it becomes the everyday adjective of large business.
items.cn: 形容词 corporate 与 corporation 及法人团体绑定。19 世纪它成为大企业的日常形容词。

items.en: Corporate culture, corporate governance and corporate identity appear as management vocabulary; corporatism names a state organised by occupational bodies.
items.cn: corporate culture、corporate governance、corporate identity 作为管理词汇出现；corporatism 指按职业团体组织起来的国家。

items.en: Modern English uses corporate mainly as an adjective. The noun is corporation, and the verb incorporate keeps the literal 'put into a body'.
items.cn: 现代英语主要把 corporate 用作形容词。名词是 corporation，动词 incorporate 保留字面义“放进一个身体里”。

note.en: The first group shares corpus 'body'; the second group separates business, collective, institutional and commercial meanings.
note.cn: 第一组共享 corpus“身体”；第二组区分商业、集体、制度和营利这几种含义。

entries.definition: relating to the body, especially physical punishment. It comes from corpus but means 'bodily', not 'of a company'.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体有关的，尤指体罚。它来自 corpus，但意思是“身体的”，不是“公司的”。

entries.definition: having a physical body; tangible. It is the philosophical cousin of corporate.
entries.definitionCN: 有实体的；物质的。它是 corporate 的哲学近亲。

entries.definition: to include something as part of a whole, or to form a legal corporation.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物纳入整体，或组成法人公司。

entries.definition: related to buying and selling for profit. It focuses on trade, while corporate focuses on the legal body.
entries.definitionCN: 与营利性买卖有关。它聚焦交易，而 corporate 聚焦法律实体。

entries.definition: shared by a group. It is broader than corporate and does not imply a legal structure.
entries.definitionCN: 群体共同拥有的。它比 corporate 更宽泛，不暗示法律结构。

entries.definition: relating to an established organisation such as a university, bank, or hospital. It is wider than corporate.
entries.definitionCN: 与大学、银行、医院等已建立的组织有关。它比 corporate 范围更广。

entries.definition: relating to trade or a company, used before nouns such as business plan. It is plainer and less legal than corporate.
entries.definitionCN: 与交易或公司有关，用于 business plan 等名词前。它比 corporate 更日常、更少法律色彩。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: corpus 'body' + -ate 'made'. Corporation, corpse, corps, corporal and incorporate all belong to the body family.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：corpus“身体”+ -ate“使成为”。corporation、corpse、corps、corporal、incorporate 都属于“身体”词族。

normal.en: corpus means body. A corporation is a group given one legal body, and corporate means belonging to that body.
normal.cn: corpus 意为身体。corporation 是被赋予一个法律身体的群体，corporate 表示属于这个身体。

normal.en: Corpse, corps, corporal and incorporate all contain the body idea: a dead body, a body of troops, bodily, and put into a body.
normal.cn: corpse、corps、corporal、incorporate 都含“身体”：尸体、军队团体、身体的、纳入身体。

normal.en: A corporate logo is the face of the legal body; corporate law is its skeleton.
normal.cn: 公司标志是法律身体的脸；公司法是它的骨架。

normal.en: Corporate culture is the personality of the body, the habits its members share.
normal.cn: 企业文化就是这个身体的性格，是成员共享的习惯。

normal.en: Incorporate means 'put into the body', whether a clause into a contract or a business into a legal form.
normal.cn: incorporate 意为“放进身体里”，无论是把条款放进合同，还是把企业放进法律形式。

abstract.en: Imagine hundreds of employees welded into one silhouette. The silhouette signs contracts, owns buildings and speaks through one logo.
abstract.cn: 想象几百名员工被焊成一个人形轮廓。这个轮廓签合同、拥有大楼，并通过一个标志说话。

abstract.en: A corporation is a body without a heartbeat: it needs a board as its brain and a charter as its spine.
abstract.cn: 公司是一个没有心跳的身体：它需要董事会当大脑、章程当脊柱。

abstract.en: The same body image can be small as a shop or large as a state; only the scale of the silhouette changes.
abstract.cn: 同一个身体意象可以小到一家店铺，大到一个国家；变的只是轮廓的大小。

examples.en: The bank announced a major corporate restructuring.
examples.cn: 这家银行宣布了大规模的公司重组。

examples.en: Corporate responsibility includes how suppliers treat their workers.
examples.cn: 企业责任包括供应商如何对待工人。

examples.en: The city acts as a corporate body when it signs the contract.
examples.cn: 这座城市签署合同时，是以法人团体的身份行事。

dict_mnemonic.text: “考破瑞特”——考破瑞特把所有人并进同一个公司身体里 → corporate 公司的、团体的

root: 拉丁语 corpus“身体”+ -ate，字面义“结成一体”，核心是“许多人合成一个法律上的身体”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of corporate, all one legal body: a company, a social power, a shared effort, a body in law, its law and finance, its face, a city, and the derived institutions built on the image.
sensesIntro.cn: corporate 的八个义项都是同一个法律身体：公司、社会力量、共同出力、法律上的团体、法律与财务、对外的脸、城市，以及由这个意象衍生的制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many people are formed into a single body that can act in law.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多人被铸成一个能在法律上行动的身体。

branches.en: COMPANY: the body as a business and as a legal-financial structure.
branches.cn: 公司：作为企业、也作为法律—财务结构的身体。

branches.en: PUBLIC FACE: a large body with power, and a body with a logo.
branches.cn: 公众面孔：拥有权力的大身体，以及带着标志的身体。

branches.en: COLLECTIVE: work and authorship belong to the body, not one hand.
branches.cn: 集体：工作与署名属于身体，而不属于某一只手。

branches.en: LEGAL STATUS: bishops, cities and charities can all be one body.
branches.cn: 法律身份：主教团、城市、慈善机构都可以是一个身体。

branches.en: DERIVED INSTITUTIONS: corporation and corporatism extend the body to economy and state.
branches.cn: 衍生制度：corporation 与 corporatism 把身体扩展到经济与国家。

intro.en: Corporate takes corpus and the suffix -ate 'made, formed'. English builds corporation with -ion and incorpor- with in-. The body image is carried by the suffix change.
intro.cn: corporate 由 corpus 加后缀 -ate“使成为”构成。英语用 -ion 构成 corporation，用 in- 构成 incorpor-。身体意象随着后缀变化被带到新词里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on corpus 'body': corpse, corps, corporal, corporeal and incorporate all describe a body or the putting of something into one.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 corpus“身体”上：corpse、corps、corporal、corporeal、incorporate 都描述身体，或把某物放进一个身体。

items.meaning: a company or group legally treated as a single body
items.meaningCN: 公司；法人团体（-ion 构成结果名词）
items.example: The corporation employs thirty thousand people.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司雇用了三万人。

items.meaning: an economic or political system organised through occupational groups
items.meaningCN: 社团主义；合作主义（-ism 构成制度或意识形态）
items.example: Corporatism gave unions a formal role in the state.
items.exampleCN: 社团主义让工会在国家中获得正式角色。

items.meaning: a supporter of corporatism; relating to it
items.meaningCN: 社团主义者；社团主义的（-ist 表示人或属性）
items.example: Corporatist policies shaped the 1930s.
items.exampleCN: 社团主义政策塑造了 20 世纪 30 年代。

items.meaning: to include something in a whole, or to form a legal corporation
items.meaningCN: 纳入；合并；组成法人（把某物放进身体）
items.example: The new rules were incorporated into the contract.
items.exampleCN: 新规则被纳入了合同。

items.meaning: the act of forming a company, or of combining things into one body
items.meaningCN: 公司设立；并入（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: Incorporation took six weeks.
items.exampleCN: 公司注册用了六周。

items.meaning: formed into a legal company, or combined into one body
items.meaningCN: 已注册为公司的；合并的（-ed 构成过去分词）
items.example: The firm is incorporated in Delaware.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司在特拉华州注册。

items.meaning: relating to a body of people organized as one
items.meaningCN: 社团的；法团的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The corporative structure gave each guild a vote.
items.exampleCN: 这种社团结构让每个行会都有一票。

items.meaning: having no physical body
items.meaningCN: 无形的；非物质的（与 corpus“身体”同根）
items.example: Rights are incorporeal property.
items.exampleCN: 权利属于无形财产。
