latinEntries.meaning: a dead body
latinEntries.meaningCN: 尸体（身体）

latinEntries.meaning: a body of troops or a group with one role
latinEntries.meaningCN: 军团；团体（一群人的身体）

latinEntries.meaning: relating to the body
latinEntries.meaningCN: 身体的（与身体有关）

latinEntries.meaning: physical, having a body
latinEntries.meaningCN: 有实体的；物质的（拥有身体）

definition_en: to match or be similar to something, or to exchange letters with someone
core_image: 两封信一来一回，内容正好对上
scene: 档案桌上摊开两份旧信件，旁边放着放大镜。 The researcher opened two old letters and found that the dates, names, and events correspond exactly.
sceneCN: 这里 correspond 是「相符、对得上」（第 1 个义项：与另一事物一致）；句意：研究员打开两份旧信件，发现日期、人名和事件完全对得上。

senses.title: Match or agree with something
senses.definition: to be in agreement with another account, fact, or set of data
senses.definitionCN: 与另一种叙述、事实或数据一致
senses.example: The witness's account corresponds with the video.
senses.exampleCN: 证人的叙述与录像相符。
senses.why: correspond is Latin com- 'together' + respondere 'to answer'. Two things correspond when each, as it were, answers the other and the answers agree.
senses.whyCN: correspond 是拉丁语 com-“相互”+ respondere“回答”。两个事物 correspond，就像各自作答，而答案正好一致。

senses.title: Be equivalent or analogous
senses.definition: to have the same function or position in a different system
senses.definitionCN: 在不同体系中具有相同功能或地位
senses.example: A captain in the navy corresponds to a colonel in the army.
senses.exampleCN: 海军上校相当于陆军上校。
senses.why: One rank answers another across systems. The equivalence is not identity but a matched reply: this post here is the counterpart of that post there.
senses.whyCN: 一个军衔在另一体系中“作答”另一个军衔。这种相当不是同一，而是对位的回应：这里的职位对应那里的职位。

senses.title: Exchange letters or messages
senses.definition: to write letters or messages to someone and receive them in return
senses.definitionCN: 与某人写信或发消息，并收到对方的回复
senses.example: They corresponded for forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们通信了四十年。
senses.why: This is the literal answering branch: a letter goes out, a letter comes back. The root's 'answer' is visible in every exchange.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面上的“回答”分支：一封信发出，一封信回来。词根里的“作答”在每一次往来中都看得见。

senses.title: Be connected in a system
senses.definition: to be linked by a fixed relationship, such as a number matching a file or a key matching a value
senses.definitionCN: 通过固定关系相连，如数字对应文件、键对应值
senses.example: Each number corresponds to a file in the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 每个编号对应档案中的一个文件。
senses.why: The 'answer back' relation becomes a mapping: one item points to its counterpart. Nothing agrees emotionally; the link is structural.
senses.whyCN: “回应”关系变成了映射：一个项目指向它的对应项。这里没有情感上的一致，联系是结构性的。

senses.title: Correspondence: letters exchanged
senses.definition: in the noun correspondence, letters written and received over time
senses.definitionCN: 名词 correspondence 表示一段时间内往来写作与收到的信件
senses.example: Their correspondence lasted forty years, and they continued to correspond until her death.
senses.exampleCN: 他们通信四十年，直到她去世前仍在相互写信。
senses.why: The noun names the collected answers. What began as a verb of replying becomes a body of letters, each one a reply to another.
senses.whyCN: 名词命名的是收集起来的“回答”。最初表示回应的动词，变成了一批信件，每一封都是对另一封的回应。

senses.title: Correspondent: one who writes or reports
senses.definition: a person who writes letters regularly, or a reporter based in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 定期写信的人，或驻在某地的记者
senses.example: She is the paper's foreign correspondent, and she corresponds from three capitals.
senses.exampleCN: 她是该报的驻外记者，从三个首都发回报道。
senses.why: A correspondent is the person who answers from a distance. The reporter sense keeps the idea of sending back dispatches to a home office.
senses.whyCN: correspondent 是从远处“作答”的人。记者义保留了“把报道发回总部”的意思。

senses.title: Corresponding: the matching counterpart
senses.definition: in the adjective corresponding, matching or connected by a regular relationship
senses.definitionCN: 形容词 corresponding 表示相匹配或通过规律性关系相连
senses.example: Sales rose, and costs fell by a corresponding amount.
senses.exampleCN: 销售额上升，成本也相应下降。
senses.why: The adjective marks the answering item in a pair. It tells the reader that another value or part exists on the other side of the relation.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记一对关系中“作答”的那一项。它告诉读者：关系的另一端还有一个对应的值或部分。

senses.title: One-to-one correspondence in mathematics
senses.definition: a relation in which every element of one set is paired with exactly one element of another
senses.definitionCN: 一个集合的每个元素与另一个集合的恰好一个元素配对的数学关系
senses.example: The two sets correspond one to one, and that correspondence proves the mapping.
senses.exampleCN: 两个集合一一对应，这种对应关系证明了该映射。
senses.why: The root's reciprocity becomes exact: every item has exactly one answer, and no answer is left unclaimed. This is correspondence at its most formal.
senses.whyCN: 词根的相互性在这里变得精确：每一项恰有一个“答案”，也没有答案无人认领。这是最形式化的对应。

intro.en: Correspond is 'answer back together'. Its stem respondere contains spondere 'to pledge', which also gives sponsor, spouse and response. The word moves from answering to matching, then to letter-writing.
intro.cn: correspond 是“一起作答”。词干 respondere 含有 spondere“许诺”，sponsor、spouse、response 也出自这里。这个词从“回答”发展到“相符”，再发展到“写信往来”。

items.en: First recorded meaning 'to be in agreement, be analogous', and also 'to exchange letters'.
items.cn: 16 世纪 20 年代最早记录，意为“一致、类似”，同时也表示“书信往来”。

items.en: From French correspondre (14c.) and Medieval Latin correspondere 'to correspond', from com- 'together' + respondere 'to answer'.
items.cn: 来自法语 correspondre（14 世纪）和中世纪拉丁语 correspondere“相应”，由 com-“一起”+ respondere“回答”构成。

items.en: respondere = re- 'back' + spondere 'to promise, pledge'. A response is literally a pledge made back to the other side.
items.cn: respondere = re-“回”+ spondere“许诺、承诺”。response 字面上就是向对方作出的回诺。

items.en: spondere also gives sponsor, spouse and responsible; the family is about binding oneself to another, not about matching shapes.
items.cn: spondere 还给出 sponsor、spouse、responsible；这个词族关于把自己与对方绑定，而不是形状相配。

items.en: Newspaper correspondent becomes a fixed role; correspondence also names a body of letters. Mathematics fixes one-to-one correspondence in the 19c.
items.cn: 报纸 correspondent 成为固定角色；correspondence 也指一批书信。数学在 19 世纪固定了 one-to-one correspondence 的说法。

items.en: Modern usage separates correspond to (match a thing or value) from correspond with (agree with a person's account, or exchange letters with a person).
items.cn: 现代用法区分 correspond to（与某物或数值对应）和 correspond with（与某人的叙述一致，或与某人通信）。

note.en: The first group shares respondere 'answer'; the second group separates matching, paralleling, counting and communicating.
note.cn: 第一组共享 respondere“回答”；第二组区分相符、平行、数目吻合与通信。

entries.definition: to answer or react. It is the simple verb inside correspond.
entries.definitionCN: 回答或反应。它就是 correspond 里面的那个简单动词。

entries.definition: having a duty to answer for something. It shares spondere 'pledge'.
entries.definitionCN: 有责任为某事作答的。它共享 spondere“许诺”。

entries.definition: letters exchanged, or a close match between things.
entries.definitionCN: 往来书信，或事物之间的高度相符。

entries.definition: to be equal, similar, or suitable. It is broader and plainer than correspond.
entries.definitionCN: 相等、相似或相配。它比 correspond 更宽泛、更日常。

entries.definition: to be similar in structure or development. It stresses two lines running side by side.
entries.definitionCN: 在结构或发展上相似。它强调两条线并排延伸。

entries.definition: to agree with another count or record. It is often used for accounts and figures.
entries.definitionCN: 与另一计数或记录相符。常用于账目和数字。

entries.definition: to exchange information. It covers the letter-writing sense but not the matching sense.
entries.definitionCN: 交换信息。它覆盖写信义，但不覆盖相符义。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: com- 'together' + respond 'answer'. Response, sponsor, spouse and responsible all come from the same pledging verb.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：com-“相互”+ respond“回答”。response、sponsor、spouse、responsible 都来自同一个“许诺”动词。

normal.en: correspond = co- 'together' + respond 'answer'. Two things correspond when their answers agree.
normal.cn: correspond = co-“相互”+ respond“回答”。两个事物的“回答”一致，就叫 correspond。

normal.en: A penfriend correspondence is literally letters answering letters over years.
normal.cn: 笔友之间的 correspondence，字面上就是多年来一封封信相互作答。

normal.en: Data correspond to a model when each value answers a prediction.
normal.cn: 当每个数值都“回答”一个预测时，数据就 correspond to 模型。

normal.en: Correspond with a person means write to them; correspond to a thing means match it.
normal.cn: correspond with 某人指写信给他；correspond to 某物指与它对应。

normal.en: A foreign correspondent answers from abroad, sending reports back to the home office.
normal.cn: 驻外 correspondent 从国外“作答”，把报道发回总部。

abstract.en: Two mirrors facing each other: whatever appears in one appears in the other, immediately and without contact.
abstract.cn: 两面相对的镜子：一面里出现什么，另一面里也出现什么，无需接触、立刻发生。

abstract.en: Two identical staircases in different buildings: no stone is shared, yet every step on one has a partner on the other.
abstract.cn: 两栋楼里有一模一样的楼梯：没有一块石头是共用的，但这一边的每一级在那边都有一个伙伴。

abstract.en: A letter is an arrow with a return address built into it. Correspondence is a field of arrows flying both ways.
abstract.cn: 一封信是一支自带回程地址的箭。书信往来就是一片双向飞行的箭。

examples.en: The written record corresponds closely to what the witnesses described.
examples.cn: 书面记录与证人描述高度吻合。

examples.en: She corresponded with a scientist in Kyoto for over a decade.
examples.cn: 她与京都的一位科学家通信十余年。

examples.en: In this table, each code corresponds to a specific region.
examples.cn: 在这张表中，每个代码对应一个特定区域。

dict_mnemonic.text: “考瑞斯邦德”——考瑞和斯邦德书信往来四十年，说法处处对得上 → correspond 通信、相符

root: 拉丁语 com-“相互”+ respondere“回答、承诺”，字面义“彼此作答”，核心是“两方一来一回正好对上”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of correspond, all one back-and-forth: accounts agree, ranks match, letters travel, values map, a collection of letters, the person who answers, the matching item, and exact one-to-one pairing.
sensesIntro.cn: correspond 的八个义项都是同一个“一来一回”：叙述相符、军衔相当、书信往返、数值映射、一批信件、作答的人、对应的一项，以及精确的一一配对。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sides answer each other, and the answers line up.
core.cn: 核心意象：两方各作答一次，答案正好对齐。

branches.en: AGREEMENT: accounts agree with each other, or ranks answer each other across two systems.
branches.cn: 一致：叙述彼此相符，或军衔在两个体系中相互对位。

branches.en: LETTERS: a written reply, and the body of letters exchanged over time.
branches.cn: 书信：书面的回复，以及一段时间内往来的一批信件。

branches.en: MAPPING: a fixed link between items, and the adjective for the matching counterpart.
branches.cn: 映射：项目之间固定的联系，以及表示对位项的形容词。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the one who writes the letters or reports from a distance.
branches.cn: 写信的人：负责通信或在远方报道的那个人。

branches.en: EXACT PAIRING: in mathematics every element answers one and only one element.
branches.cn: 精确配对：数学中每个元素只回答一个元素，且只回答一个。

intro.en: Correspond adds -ence for the letters or the match, -ent for the person, and -ing/-ly for the matching adjective and adverb.
intro.cn: correspond 加 -ence 表示信件或相符，加 -ent 表示人，加 -ing/-ly 构成对应的形容词和副词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on spondere 'to pledge': response, sponsor, spouse and responsible all bind one party to another.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 spondere“许诺”上：response、sponsor、spouse、responsible 都把一方与另一方绑定。

items.meaning: letters exchanged; a close match
items.meaningCN: 通信；往来信件；相符（-ence 构成状态或结果名词）
items.example: The correspondence between the two reports is striking.
items.exampleCN: 两份报告之间的吻合令人惊讶。

items.meaning: a person who writes letters or reports from a place
items.meaningCN: 通信者；驻外记者（-ent 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The correspondent filed a story from the border.
items.exampleCN: 驻外记者从边境发回了报道。

items.meaning: matching or paired with something else
items.meaningCN: 相应的；对应的（-ing 分词作形容词）
items.example: Open the corresponding file on the second screen.
items.exampleCN: 在第二个屏幕上打开相应的文件。

items.meaning: in a matching way
items.meaningCN: 相应地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Prices rose and demand fell correspondingly.
items.exampleCN: 价格上涨，需求也相应下降。

items.meaning: matched, or exchanged letters
items.meaningCN: 相符过的；通信过的（-ed 构成过去式）
items.example: The two accounts corresponded exactly.
items.exampleCN: 两份记录完全吻合。

items.meaning: answering or matching another thing
items.meaningCN: 应答的；对应的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The two clauses are corresponsive.
items.exampleCN: 这两个从句彼此呼应。

items.meaning: an answer or reaction
items.meaningCN: 回应；反应（与 spondere“许诺”同根）
items.example: Her response came by email.
items.exampleCN: 她的回复是通过邮件发来的。

items.meaning: a person or firm that promises support
items.meaningCN: 赞助者；发起人（同出 spondere“郑重许诺”）
items.example: A local bank is the sponsor of the race.
items.exampleCN: 一家本地银行是这场赛跑的赞助方。

latinEntries.meaning: an answer or reaction
latinEntries.meaningCN: 回答；反应（回过来的承诺）

latinEntries.meaning: a person or firm that promises support
latinEntries.meaningCN: 赞助者；发起人（作出承诺的人）

latinEntries.meaning: a husband or wife, one bound by a promise
latinEntries.meaningCN: 配偶（被承诺绑定的人）

latinEntries.meaning: answerable for something; reliable
latinEntries.meaningCN: 有责任的；可靠的（能够作出回应）

definition_zh: 创造；创建；创作；引起；授予（头衔）
definition_en: to make something new exist, to produce a work or an effect, or to give someone a new rank
core_image: 空桌上落下第一笔，东西从无到有
scene: 白板上写下了第一行产品蓝图，团队的草图摊在桌上。 The team wrote the first line of the product plan on the whiteboard; they were about to create a new booking system.
sceneCN: 这里 create 是「创建、创造」（第 1 个义项：使新事物出现）；句意：团队在白板上写下产品蓝图的第一行，即将创建一个全新的预约系统。

pos.zh: 创造；创建；创作；引起；授予

senses.title: Bring something new into existence
senses.definition: to make something exist that did not exist before
senses.definitionCN: 使原本不存在的东西开始存在
senses.example: The lab created a new battery material.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室创造了一种新的电池材料。
senses.why: Latin creare meant 'to make, bring forth, produce, beget'. The image is not assembly from parts but a new thing coming into being, as a plant is brought forth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 creare 意为“制造、生出、生产、生育”。意象不是把零件组装起来，而是一个新东西被“生出来”，像植物长出来一样。

senses.title: Make a work of art or composition
senses.definition: to make a painting, piece of music, story, or other work by imagination and skill
senses.definitionCN: 凭想象与技艺创作绘画、音乐、故事等作品
senses.example: The composer created a symphony in three months.
senses.exampleCN: 作曲家用了三个月创作出一部交响曲。
senses.why: creare applies to deliberate making. The maker brings forth a whole that did not exist, but the material and the craft are both present.
senses.whyCN: creare 也用于有意的制作。创作者生出一个原本不存在的整体，但材料与技艺同时在场。

senses.title: Cause an effect or situation
senses.definition: to cause a state, problem, or feeling to begin to exist
senses.definitionCN: 使某种状态、问题或感觉开始存在
senses.example: The delay created uncertainty in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 延误在市场里造成了不确定性。
senses.why: What is brought forth can be a state rather than an object. Uncertainty is 'made to exist' by the delay, exactly as an object is made to exist by a maker.
senses.whyCN: 被生出的可以是一种状态，而不是一个物件。不确定性被延误“造了出来”，正如物件被制造者造出来。

senses.title: Establish an institution or position
senses.definition: to establish an organisation, role, or rule by official decision
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式决定设立组织、职位或规则
senses.example: The university created a chair in climate science.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学设立了一个气候科学教席。
senses.why: Institutions are brought into being by decision, not by physical labour. The word treats a role or office as something that can be 'made' and then filled.
senses.whyCN: 机构是通过决定被“生出”的，而不是通过体力劳动。这个词把一个职位或机构当作可以被“造出来”、再有人坐上去的东西。

senses.title: Appoint or give a new rank
senses.definition: in formal or historical usage, to give someone a new title or rank
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或历史用法中，授予某人新的头衔或等级
senses.example: The king created him a baron.
senses.exampleCN: 国王封他为男爵。
senses.why: Latin creare also meant 'to elect, appoint'. A new status is made by authority, so the person's rank is brought into existence by the sovereign's word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 creare 也有“选举、任命”义。新身份由权威“造出”，因此一个人的等级由君主的一句话被带入存在。

senses.title: Divine creation
senses.definition: in religious language, to bring the universe or life into being
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教语言中，使宇宙或生命出现
senses.example: Many traditions say a god created the world.
senses.exampleCN: 许多传统说一位神创造了世界。
senses.why: This is the ultimate 'bring forth': existence itself is made. Theology adds creatio ex nihilo, creation out of nothing, which pushes the image to its limit.
senses.whyCN: 这是最极端的“生出”：存在本身被造出来。神学加上 creatio ex nihilo（从无中创造），把这个意象推到极限。

senses.title: Creative: able to bring forth
senses.titleCN: 有创造力的：能够生出新东西
senses.definition: in the adjective creative, able to produce original ideas or works
senses.definitionCN: 形容词 creative 表示能够产生原创想法或作品
senses.example: Creative work needs freedom, and freedom is what lets a team create.
senses.exampleCN: 创造性工作需要自由，而自由正是让团队能够创造的东西。
senses.why: The adjective names the capacity behind creare. A creative person is one in whom new things can be brought forth.
senses.whyCN: 形容词命名 creare 背后的能力。有创造力的人，就是新东西能在其内部被生出来的人。

senses.title: Creation: the act or the thing made
senses.definition: in the noun creation, the act of creating or the thing that results
senses.definitionCN: 名词 creation 表示创造行为或创造出来的东西
senses.example: The creation of the park took ten years, and the city had to create a trust to pay for it.
senses.exampleCN: 这座公园的建成用了十年，市政府不得不设立一个信托来支付费用。
senses.why: The noun covers both the bringing forth and what was brought forth. English does not force a choice between the act and its result.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词同时覆盖“生出”的行为和被生出的东西。英语不强迫人在行为与结果之间二选一。

senses.title: Creator: the one who brings forth
senses.titleCN: 创造者：生出新东西的人
senses.definition: in the noun creator, the person who makes or originates something
senses.definitionCN: 名词 creator 表示制造或创始某物的人
senses.example: The creator of the app sold it to a bank, which then created its own version.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用的创建者把它卖给了银行，银行随后做出了自己的版本。
senses.why: Every bringing-forth has a source. The -or suffix turns the verb into the person at the moment of origin.
senses.whyCN: 每一次“生出”都有一个源头。-or 后缀把动词变成“处在起源时刻的那个人”。

intro.en: Create is a 'growing' word: Latin creare 'bring forth' is related to crescere 'grow' and to Ceres, the goddess of growth. The deepest PIE link is generally accepted, not certain.
intro.cn: create 是一个“生长”词：拉丁语 creare“生出”与 crescere“生长”以及谷物女神 Ceres 有关。最深的原始印欧语联系属于一般认为是，并非确证。

items.en: First recorded meaning 'to make, bring forth, produce'. The theological sense 'create the world' is among the earliest uses.
items.cn: 14 世纪晚期最早记录，意为“制造、生出、生产”。“创造世界”的神学义属于最早用法之一。

items.en: From Latin creatus, past participle of creare 'to make, bring forth, produce, beget'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 creatus，即 creare“制造、生出、生产、生育”的过去分词。

items.en: creare is related to crescere 'to arise, grow' and to Ceres, the goddess of grain and growth; creature is literally 'a thing made'.
items.cn: creare 与 crescere“产生、生长”以及谷物与生长女神 Ceres 有关；creature 字面就是“被造出来的东西”。

items.en: The family is traced to PIE *ker- (2) 'to grow'. The reconstruction is generally accepted, and the exact path from 'grow' to 'create' is not fully settled.
items.cn: 这个词族被追溯到原始印欧语 *ker-（第 2 义）“生长”。该重构属于一般认为是，从“生长”到“创造”的确切路径也尚未完全定论。

items.en: Artistic creation becomes a standard phrase; 'create a position' and 'create jobs' extend the verb to institutions and employment.
items.cn: artistic creation 成为固定说法；create a position 与 create jobs 把动词扩展到机构与就业。

items.en: Modern English keeps the whole family: create, creation, creator, creative, creativity and creature. The core sense is still 'bring forth something new'.
items.cn: 现代英语保留整个词族：create、creation、creator、creative、creativity、creature。核心义仍是“生出新东西”。

note.en: The first group shares creare 'make, grow'; the second group separates general making, production, invention and generation.
note.cn: 第一组共享 creare“制造、生长”；第二组区分一般制造、生产、发明和生成。

entries.definition: a living being, literally 'a thing made'. It is the noun relative of create.
entries.definitionCN: 生物，字面义“被造出来的东西”。它是 create 的名词同族词。

entries.definition: able to produce original work or ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 有创造力的；能产生原创作品或想法的。

entries.definition: the act of bringing something into being, or the thing made.
entries.definitionCN: 创造行为，或被造出来的东西。

entries.definition: to form or produce something. It is the broadest verb and does not imply novelty.
entries.definitionCN: 形成或生产某物。它是最宽泛的动词，不暗示新颖。

entries.definition: to make goods or bring about a result, often in quantity. It stresses output rather than new existence.
entries.definitionCN: 生产商品或产生结果，常指批量。它强调产出，而不是“全新存在”。

entries.definition: to design something that did not exist before, especially a device or method. It is narrower than create.
entries.definitionCN: 设计出原本不存在的东西，尤指装置或方法。它比 create 窄。

entries.definition: to cause something to arise, such as power, income, or ideas. It often implies a process rather than a maker.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物产生，如电力、收入或想法。它常暗示过程，而不是创造者。

normalIntro.en: Real family: creare 'bring forth' links create with creation, creator, creative, creativity and creature; crescere 'grow' and Ceres belong to the same growth cluster.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词族：creare“生出”把 create 与 creation、creator、creative、creativity、creature 连在一起；crescere“生长”和 Ceres 属于同一个“生长”群。

normal.en: creare means bring forth. A creature is literally something brought forth, and a creator is the one who brings it.
normal.cn: creare 意为生出。creature 字面上就是被生出的东西，creator 就是生出它的人。

normal.en: Ceres, the goddess of grain, shares the growth idea: what is created is made to grow into existence.
normal.cn: 谷物女神 Ceres 共享“生长”观念：被创造的东西是被“长”出来的。

normal.en: Create a position and create jobs show that an institution or a role can be brought into being by decision.
normal.cn: create a position 和 create jobs 说明，机构或职位可以通过决定被带入存在。

normal.en: The king created him a baron: a rank is made, not inherited, in this older sense.
normal.cn: “the king created him a baron”：在这个旧义里，等级是被“造出”的，不是继承的。

normal.en: Creation, creator, creative, creativity and creature all sit inside one family, because they all answer 'what was brought forth?'
normal.cn: creation、creator、creative、creativity、creature 都在同一个词族里，因为它们都回答“什么被生出来了？”。

abstract.en: A blank canvas with one stroke on it: before the stroke there was nothing, after it there is a direction.
abstract.cn: 一张空白画布上落下第一笔：落笔之前什么都没有，落笔之后有了一个方向。

abstract.en: A seed splitting open is creation without a craftsman: the new plant is brought forth from what was already there.
abstract.cn: 种子裂开是一种没有工匠的创造：新植物从已有的东西里被生出来。

abstract.en: Creation and creature are the two ends of one event: the act of bringing forth, and the thing that now exists.
abstract.cn: creation 与 creature 是同一件事的两端：生出的动作，以及如今存在的东西。

examples.en: The new policy created thousands of jobs in the region.
examples.cn: 新政策在该地区创造了数千个就业岗位。

examples.en: She created a small garden out of a bare yard.
examples.cn: 她在一片空院子里造出了一个小花园。

examples.en: The artist creates by choosing what to leave out.
examples.cn: 艺术家通过选择“省略什么”来创作。

dict_mnemonic.text: “克瑞特”——克瑞特在空桌上做出第一版产品 → create 创造、创建

root: 拉丁语 creare“创造、生出”，与 crescere“生长”同源，核心是“让原本不存在的东西长出来”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of create, all one bringing-forth: a new thing, a work of art, an effect, an institution, a rank, the world, the creative capacity, the act or result, and the creator.
sensesIntro.cn: create 的九个义项都是同一个“生出”：新事物、艺术作品、效果、机构、头衔、世界、创造能力、行为或结果，以及创造者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something is brought forth from nothing or from raw material.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物从无中、或从原料中被生出来。

branches.en: MAKING: a new object or a new work is brought into being.
branches.cn: 制造：新物件或新作品被带入存在。

branches.en: CAUSATION: a state or feeling can be made to exist.
branches.cn: 因果：状态或感觉也可以被造出来。

branches.en: INSTITUTION: a role, office, or rank is created by decision.
branches.cn: 制度：职位、机构或等级由决定造出。

branches.en: ORIGIN AND CAPACITY: divine creation, and the human power to bring forth.
branches.cn: 起源与能力：神的创造，以及人“生出”的力量。

branches.en: ACT AND AGENT: creation names the event or result; creator names its source.
branches.cn: 行为与施事：creation 命名事件或结果；creator 命名源头。

intro.en: create takes -ion for creation, -or for creator, -ive for creative and -ivity for creativity. The Latin root creare is not productive by itself in English.
intro.cn: create 加 -ion 构成 creation，加 -or 构成 creator，加 -ive 构成 creative，加 -ivity 构成 creativity。拉丁词根 creare 本身在英语中不独立能产。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on creare 'bring forth' and crescere 'grow': creature, crescent, increase and concrete (grown together) all carry the growth image.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 creare“生出”和 crescere“生长”上：creature、crescent、increase、concrete（长在一起）都带着生长意象。

items.meaning: the act of creating, or the thing created
items.meaningCN: 创造；创作；创造物（-ion 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: The creation of the museum took a decade.
items.exampleCN: 这座博物馆的创建花了十年。

items.meaning: a person who makes or originates something
items.meaningCN: 创造者；创作者（-or 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The creator of the game remains anonymous.
items.exampleCN: 这个游戏的创造者仍然匿名。

items.meaning: able to produce original ideas or works
items.meaningCN: 有创造力的（-ive 表示倾向或能力）
items.example: The team needed a creative solution.
items.exampleCN: 团队需要一个有创意的解决方案。

items.meaning: the ability to create
items.meaningCN: 创造力（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The workshop is designed to spark creativity.
items.exampleCN: 这个工作坊旨在激发创造力。

items.meaning: lacking originality
items.meaningCN: 缺乏创造力的（un- 表否定）
items.example: The routine is efficient but uncreative.
items.exampleCN: 这套流程效率高但缺乏创造性。

items.meaning: brought into being
items.meaningCN: 被创造的（-ed 构成过去分词）
items.example: The position was created last year.
items.exampleCN: 这个职位是去年设立的。

items.meaning: the act of bringing something into being
items.meaningCN: 创造（动名词）；正在创造（现在分词）
items.example: Creating a new habit takes time.
items.exampleCN: 养成新习惯需要时间。

items.meaning: to make something exist again
items.meaningCN: 再创造；重现（re- 表再次）
items.example: The film tries to recreate the 1920s.
items.exampleCN: 这部影片试图重现二十世纪二十年代。

latinEntries.meaning: a living being, something made
latinEntries.meaningCN: 生物；造物（被生出的东西）

latinEntries.meaning: growing; a shape that looks like a growing moon
latinEntries.meaningCN: 新月形的（正在生长的）

latinEntries.meaning: to become larger
latinEntries.meaningCN: 增加（向上生长）

latinEntries.meaning: grown together; solid and real
latinEntries.meaningCN: 具体的；混凝土（长在一起的实体）

definition_zh: 信用；赊购；贷方；学分；赞扬；相信；归功于
definition_en: trust or belief; permission to pay later; a unit of study; praise or recognition; to believe or attribute
core_image: 账簿上被记在“可信”一侧的一笔
scene: 成绩单上列着学分栏，旁边盖着教务印章。 She had earned enough credits to meet the graduation requirement.
sceneCN: 这里 credit 是「学分」（第 6 个义项：课程学习计量单位）；句意：她已经修满足够的学分，符合毕业要求。

pos.zh: 信用；赊购；贷方；学分；赞扬

collocations.zh: 认为某人具有（某种品质或功劳）

senses.title: Belief or trust in a statement
senses.titleCN: 相信：对某种说法的信任
senses.definition: the belief that something is true, or trust in a person's account
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事为真的信念，或对某人叙述的信任
senses.example: The theory slowly gained credit among physicists.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论逐渐赢得了物理学家的信任。
senses.why: Latin credere meant 'to trust, believe, entrust'. Credit is trust treated as something that can be given and received, like a substance in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 credere 意为“信任、相信、托付”。credit 就是被当作可以给出和接收的“信任”，像头脑里的一种物质。

senses.title: Reputation for trustworthiness
senses.definition: the good reputation a person or organisation has for honesty and reliability
senses.definitionCN: 个人或组织因诚实可靠而拥有的好名声
senses.example: The firm's credit suffered after the scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻之后，这家公司的信誉受损。
senses.why: Repeated trust hardens into reputation. Credit is no longer one act of believing but the standing a name has earned over time.
senses.whyCN: 反复的信任会凝固成声誉。credit 不再是某一次相信，而是一个名字长期挣得的名声地位。

senses.title: Permission to pay later
senses.definition: an arrangement in which goods or services are given now and paid for later
senses.definitionCN: 现在先给货或服务、以后付款的安排
senses.example: They bought the furniture on credit.
senses.exampleCN: 他们赊购了这套家具。
senses.why: The seller trusts the buyer to pay. Trust becomes a financial instrument: the goods travel now, the money travels later.
senses.whyCN: 卖家信任买家会付款。信任变成了一种金融工具：货物现在过去，钱以后过去。

senses.title: Money added to an account
senses.definition: in bookkeeping, an amount entered on the credit side of an account; to add money to an account
senses.definitionCN: 簿记中记在账户贷方的一笔金额；把钱记入账户
senses.example: The refund was credited to her account.
senses.exampleCN: 退款被记入了她的账户。
senses.why: Accounting calls the trusted side the credit side. Money that the account receives is entered there, so the verb credit means 'put on the trusted side'.
senses.whyCN: 会计把受信任的一侧称为贷方。账户收到的钱记在这一侧，因此动词 credit 的意思是“记到可信的一侧”。

senses.title: Borrowing capacity and credit score
senses.definition: the amount a person or company is trusted to borrow, measured by a credit rating or score
senses.definitionCN: 个人或公司被信任可借的额度，用信用评级或评分衡量
senses.example: A low score limits your credit.
senses.exampleCN: 评分低会限制你的信贷额度。
senses.why: Trust is quantified. A score turns the question 'do we believe you will pay?' into a number that lenders can compare.
senses.whyCN: 信任被量化。评分把“我们相信你会还钱吗？”变成放贷人可以比较的一个数字。

senses.title: Academic credit: a unit of study
senses.definition: a unit that counts the amount of study a student has completed
senses.definitionCN: 计算学生已完成学习量的单位
senses.example: The course is worth three credits.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课值三个学分。
senses.why: 19c American education turned completed work into countable evidence. A credit is a unit of trustworthy proof that a student did the work.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪美国教育把完成的学习变成可计数的证据。一个学分就是“学生确实做过这份功课”的可信证明单位。

senses.title: Praise and recognition
senses.definition: approval or recognition given to someone for an achievement
senses.definitionCN: 因某项成就而给予某人的赞许或认可
senses.example: She took credit for the idea.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这个主意归功于自己。
senses.why: Social credit is belief about who caused a good result. To give credit is to say 'we believe this came from you', so praise and attribution share one word.
senses.whyCN: 社会性的 credit 是关于“好结果由谁造成”的相信。give credit 就是说“我们相信这出自你”，因此赞扬与归功共用同一个词。

senses.title: Film credits
senses.definition: the list of names at the end of a film or programme, showing who worked on it
senses.definitionCN: 电影或节目结尾列出的工作人员姓名表
senses.example: The credits list every grip and driver.
senses.exampleCN: 片尾字幕列出了每位场务和司机。
senses.why: A film is a collective product, and the credits distribute belief about who made what. Each name is a small public credit entry.
senses.whyCN: 电影是集体产品，片尾字幕分配“谁做了什么”的相信。每个名字都是一小笔公开的 credit 记录。

senses.title: To one's credit: as a good quality
senses.titleCN: 值得称赞的是：作为优点
senses.definition: in the phrase to someone's credit, as something that deserves approval
senses.definitionCN: 短语 to someone's credit 表示某件事值得赞许
senses.example: To his credit, he admitted the error at once.
senses.exampleCN: 值得称赞的是，他立刻承认了错误。
senses.why: The phrase puts a quality on the person's trusted side of the ledger. It is an accounting image used for moral bookkeeping.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把某种品质记到个人账簿上“可信”的一侧。它是把记账意象用在道德账本上。

senses.title: Verb: believe or attribute
senses.definition: to believe that something is true, or to say that someone is responsible for something
senses.definitionCN: 相信某事为真，或认为某事应归功于某人
senses.example: The discovery is credited to a student.
senses.exampleCN: 这项发现被归功于一名学生。
senses.why: The verb applies the same trust to a statement or a person. Crediting a student is publicly entering the student's name on the trusted side of the record.
senses.whyCN: 动词把同一种信任用在说法或人身上。credit 一名学生，就是把他的名字公开记到记录的“可信”一侧。

intro.en: Credit is a trust word. Latin credere 'believe, entrust' is related to cor 'heart', so the oldest image is giving someone your heart. Commerce later turned that trust into a payment arrangement.
intro.cn: credit 是一个“信任”词。拉丁语 credere“相信、托付”与 cor“心”有关，最早的意象是“把心交给对方”。商业后来把这种信任变成付款安排。

items.en: First recorded meaning 'belief, faith, trust', borrowed through French from Italian commercial usage.
items.cn: 16 世纪 20 年代最早记录，意为“相信、信念、信任”，经法语借入，带有意大利商业用语的痕迹。

items.en: French crédit (15c.) 'belief, trust' and Italian credito both go back to Latin creditum 'a loan, a thing entrusted to another'.
items.cn: 法语 crédit（15 世纪）“相信、信任”和意大利语 credito 都可上溯到拉丁语 creditum“贷款、托付给他人之物”。

items.en: creditum is the neuter past participle of credere 'to trust, entrust, believe'. In Latin, a creditor is someone who trusts another with money.
items.cn: creditum 是 credere“信任、托付、相信”的中性过去分词。在拉丁语里，creditor 就是把钱托付给别人、相信对方的人。

items.en: credere is related to cor 'heart' (PIE *kerd- 'heart'), the same family as cardiac and courage. The link is generally accepted.
items.cn: credere 与 cor“心”有关（原始印欧语 *kerd-“心”），与 cardiac、courage 同族。这一联系属于一般认为是。

items.en: Commercial credit (trust in later payment) appears in the 16c.; credit as reputation in the 17c.; bookkeeping credit and academic credit in the 19c.
items.cn: 商业信用（相信对方以后付款）见于 16 世纪；表示声誉的 credit 见于 17 世纪；簿记贷方与学分见于 19 世纪。

items.en: Modern English adds credit card, credit rating and film credits. Credible, creditor and credibility keep the trust idea in separate words.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了 credit card、credit rating 和 film credits。credible、creditor、credibility 把“信任”观念保留在独立词里。

note.en: The first group shares credere 'believe' or looks close to it; the second group separates trust, borrowing, recognition and belief.
note.cn: 第一组共享 credere“相信”或词形接近；第二组区分信任、借贷、认可和信念。

entries.definition: a person or bank to whom money is owed. It is the one who has trusted another with money.
entries.definitionCN: 被欠钱的人或银行。就是把钱托付给别人、相信对方的人。

entries.definition: believable, able to be trusted. It turns the verb 'believe' into a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 可信的；值得信任的。它把动词“相信”变成一种性质。

entries.definition: a set of beliefs, especially religious. It comes from credo 'I believe'.
entries.definitionCN: 信条，尤指宗教信条。它来自 credo“我相信”。

entries.definition: firm belief in someone's honesty or reliability. It is the feeling behind credit.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人诚实或可靠的坚定相信。它是 credit 背后的情感基础。

entries.definition: money lent that must be paid back. It is the object, while credit is the permission or trust.
entries.definitionCN: 借出、必须归还的钱。它是对象，而 credit 是许可或信任。

entries.definition: public approval for an achievement. It overlaps credit in the praise sense.
entries.definitionCN: 对成就的公开认可。它在“赞扬”义上与 credit 重叠。

entries.definition: the feeling that something is true. It is the general mental state; credit is belief given social or financial form.
entries.definitionCN: 认为某事为真的感觉。它是一般心理状态；credit 是把相信赋予社会或金融形式。

normalIntro.en: Real family: credere 'believe' gives credit, credible, creditor, creed and credibility. cor 'heart' links it to cardiac and courage.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词族：credere“相信”给出 credit、credible、creditor、creed、credibility。cor“心”把它与 cardiac、courage 连起来。

normal.en: credere means believe. Credit is belief turned into something you can give: give credit, gain credit, lose credit.
normal.cn: credere 意为相信。credit 是变成“可以给予”的相信：give credit、gain credit、lose credit。

normal.en: On credit means the seller believes you will pay later. The whole phrase is trust in action.
normal.cn: on credit 指卖家相信你以后会付款。整个短语就是“信任”在行动。

normal.en: A creditor is the one who trusts; a debtor is the one trusted. Both words come from the same belief.
normal.cn: creditor 是给出信任的人，debtor 是被信任的人。两个词都出自同一种“相信”。

normal.en: To take credit for something is to claim that the belief about who did it should point at you.
normal.cn: “take credit for something”就是主张“这事是谁做的”那份相信应当指向自己。

normal.en: Academic credit and film credits both count names: one counts work done, the other counts who did it.
normal.cn: 学分和片尾字幕都在“计数名字”：一个计算完成的功课，一个记录是谁做的。

abstract.en: Picture a heart handed across a table as a deposit. That is the oldest shape of credit: belief offered before proof.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗心被放到桌上当定金。这是 credit 最老的形状：在证据之前先给出相信。

abstract.en: A ledger has two sides. Credit is the side where good things are entered, whether money or merit.
abstract.cn: 账簿有两边。credit 是记录“好事情”的那一边，不管是钱还是功劳。

abstract.en: Modern finance has turned trust into a number. The number is not the trust, only its shadow.
abstract.cn: 现代金融把信任变成了一个数字。数字不是信任本身，只是信任的影子。

examples.en: The supplier agreed to deliver the goods on credit.
examples.cn: 供应商同意赊账发货。

examples.en: She deserves credit for holding the team together.
examples.cn: 她把团队凝聚在一起，值得赞扬。

examples.en: The payment was credited to the wrong account.
examples.cn: 这笔付款被记入了错误的账户。

dict_mnemonic.text: “克瑞迪特”——克瑞迪特凭信任先拿货、月底再付钱 → credit 信用、赊账

root: 拉丁语 credere“相信、托付”，与 cor“心”同源，核心是“把信任交出去”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of credit, all one trust: belief, reputation, deferred payment, an account entry, borrowing power, a study unit, praise, screen names, a moral entry, and the verb that believes or attributes.
sensesIntro.cn: credit 的十个义项都是同一种信任：相信、信誉、赊购、记账、借贷能力、学分、赞扬、片尾名单、道德账本，以及表示“相信或归功”的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: trust is entered on a ledger, and what is trusted is marked as good.
core.cn: 核心意象：信任被记入账簿，被信任的东西被标在“好”的一侧。

branches.en: BELIEF AND REPUTATION: trust in a statement hardens into a name.
branches.cn: 相信与声誉：对说法的信任凝固成一个名字。

branches.en: FINANCE: payment later, entries in an account, and a measured borrowing limit.
branches.cn: 金融：以后付款、账户记录，以及被量化的借款额度。

branches.en: COUNTING: credits count study and count the people who made a film.
branches.cn: 计数：学分计算学习量，片尾字幕计算参与制作的人。

branches.en: MERIT: praise and 'to one's credit' are moral entries on the same ledger.
branches.cn: 功劳：赞扬与 to one's credit 是同一账簿上的道德记录。

branches.en: VERB: to credit is to believe, or to put a name on the trusted side.
branches.cn: 动词：credit 表示相信，或把某个名字记到可信的一侧。

intro.en: credit takes -or for the person who trusts, -ible for 'able to be believed', -ibility for the quality, and -able for 'deserving praise'.
intro.cn: credit 加 -or 表示给出信任的人，加 -ible 表示“可被相信的”，加 -ibility 表示性质，加 -able 表示“值得赞扬的”。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on credere 'believe': creed, credo, credential and incredible all involve what can or cannot be believed.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 credere“相信”上：creed、credo、credential、incredible 都涉及“可信或不可信”。

items.meaning: a person or institution to whom money is owed
items.meaningCN: 债权人；贷方（-or 表示给出信任的人）
items.example: The creditor agreed to extend the deadline.
items.exampleCN: 债权人同意延长期限。

items.meaning: able to be believed or trusted
items.meaningCN: 可信的（-ible 表示“能够被……”）
items.example: The witness gave a credible account.
items.exampleCN: 证人提供了可信的叙述。

items.meaning: the quality of being believed
items.meaningCN: 可信度（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The error damaged the report's credibility.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误损害了报告的可信度。

items.meaning: deserving praise or approval
items.meaningCN: 值得赞扬的（-able 表示值得）
items.example: She made a creditable attempt under pressure.
items.exampleCN: 她在压力下做出了值得称赞的尝试。

items.meaning: believed, or entered in an account
items.meaningCN: 归功于；记入账户的（-ed 构成过去分词）
items.example: The discovery was credited to her team.
items.exampleCN: 这项发现被归功于她的团队。

items.meaning: the act of entering an amount or giving recognition
items.meaningCN: 贷记；归功（动名词，也是现在分词）
items.example: Crediting the account takes one day.
items.exampleCN: 把款项记入账户需要一天。

items.meaning: impossible to believe
items.meaningCN: 难以置信的（in- 表否定）
items.example: The view from the ridge is incredible.
items.exampleCN: 山脊上的景色令人难以置信。

items.meaning: a document proving trustworthiness or qualification
items.meaningCN: 资格证书；凭证（-ential 构成名词）
items.example: She showed her credentials at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 她在门口出示了证件。

latinEntries.meaning: a statement of belief
latinEntries.meaningCN: 信条（“我相信”的陈述）

latinEntries.meaning: evidence that one can be trusted or is qualified
latinEntries.meaningCN: 资历证明（证明可信或有资格）

latinEntries.meaning: impossible to believe; also astonishing
latinEntries.meaningCN: 难以置信的；惊人的（不可信）

latinEntries.meaning: a set of beliefs or a statement of them
latinEntries.meaningCN: 信条；信念（拉丁语“我相信”）

definition_en: plural of criterion: the standards by which something is judged or decided
core_image: 一把用来筛人的筛子，孔的大小就是标准
scene: 面试桌上堆着简历，筛选表列着三条硬性条件。 The HR officer wrote three hard criteria into the screening form.
sceneCN: 这里 criteria 是「标准、准则」（第 1 个义项：判断事物的依据，复数）；句意：人力资源专员把三条硬性标准写进了筛选表。

senses.title: Standards used for judging
senses.definition: the standards or rules by which something is judged, compared, or decided
senses.definitionCN: 用来判断、比较或决定某事物的标准或规则
senses.example: The judges scored the entries against five criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 评委按五条标准给参赛作品打分。
senses.why: Greek kritērion meant 'means for judging', from krinein 'to separate, decide'. Criteria are the tools that separate the good from the bad, the eligible from the not.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 kritērion 意为“判断的工具”，来自 krinein“分开、决定”。criteria 就是把人或事物分成好坏、合格与不合格的工具。

senses.title: Singular and plural: criterion, criteria
senses.titleCN: 单数与复数：criterion 与 criteria
senses.definition: criteria is the plural of criterion; 'a criteria' is nonstandard because criteria already means more than one
senses.definitionCN: criteria 是 criterion 的复数；“a criteria”不合标准，因为 criteria 本身已表示多个
senses.example: One criterion, two criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 一个标准是 criterion，两个标准是 criteria。
senses.why: criterion is a Greek neuter noun in -on, and Greek neuters of this type take -a in the plural. The plural therefore has no -s: kriterion becomes kritēria.
senses.whyCN: criterion 是希腊语中以 -on 结尾的中性名词，这类希腊中性名词的复数用 -a。因此复数不加 -s：kriterion 变成 kritēria。

senses.title: Selection and admission criteria
senses.definition: the published standards used to choose among applicants
senses.definitionCN: 用于在申请者中挑选的公开标准
senses.example: The scholarship has clear selection criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 这项奖学金有明确的选拔标准。
senses.why: An institution applies the sieve publicly so that the decision can be defended. Criteria make a choice look less arbitrary.
senses.whyCN: 机构公开使用这把筛子，使决定可以被辩护。标准让选择看起来不那么任意。

senses.title: Diagnostic criteria in medicine
senses.definition: the agreed set of symptoms and tests that must be present before a diagnosis is made
senses.definitionCN: 作出诊断前必须出现的、经同行约定的症状与检查指标
senses.example: The diagnosis follows international criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 诊断遵循国际标准。
senses.why: Medicine separates symptoms into categories that decide a case. The Greek root's 'separate and decide' is here a clinical procedure.
senses.whyCN: 医学把症状分进不同类别，以此决定病例。希腊词根的“分开并判定”在这里是一项临床程序。

senses.title: Design and quality criteria
senses.definition: the measurable requirements a product or structure must meet
senses.definitionCN: 产品或结构必须满足的可测量要求
senses.example: The bridge was tested against safety criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥按安全标准进行了测试。
senses.why: Engineering turns judgement into numbers so that pass or fail can be checked. The criteria are the ruler laid against the object.
senses.whyCN: 工程把判断变成数字，使合格与否可以被检查。标准就是贴在对象上的那把尺。

senses.title: Eligibility criteria
senses.definition: the conditions a person must satisfy to qualify for a benefit, programme, or right
senses.definitionCN: 个人为获得福利、项目或权利必须满足的条件
senses.example: Applicants must meet the eligibility criteria.
senses.exampleCN: 申请人必须符合资格标准。
senses.why: This is the legal sieve: it separates those entitled from those not. The decision is made before any individual case is heard.
senses.whyCN: 这是法律筛子：它把有资格的人和无资格的人分开。决定在个案被听取之前就已由标准作出。

senses.title: Acceptance criteria in projects
senses.definition: the predefined conditions that must be met before work is accepted as complete
senses.definitionCN: 工作被接受为完成之前必须满足的预定条件
senses.example: A task is done when its acceptance criteria are met.
senses.exampleCN: 当验收标准满足时，任务才算完成。
senses.why: Project management fixes the standards before the work starts. The criteria decide when the deliverable is accepted, so 'done' becomes a judgement with a rule.
senses.whyCN: 项目管理在开工前先固定标准。标准决定交付物何时被接受，于是“完成”变成一个有规则的判断。

senses.title: Research and measurement criteria
senses.definition: the rules used to decide which data or methods count as valid in a study
senses.definitionCN: 用于判定哪些数据或方法在研究中等效的规则
senses.example: The study defined criteria for valid samples.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究为有效样本设定了标准。
senses.why: Research separates usable evidence from noise. Criteria are the stated conditions under which a sample or result is admitted.
senses.whyCN: 研究把可用证据与噪声分开。标准就是宣布样本或结果被接纳时所依据的条件。

senses.title: Greek -on/-a plurals
senses.definition: the morphological pattern in which Greek neuter nouns ending in -on form their plural in -a
senses.definitionCN: 以 -on 结尾的希腊中性名词用 -a 构成复数的词形模式
senses.example: Criterion/criteria follows the Greek pattern, like phenomenon/phenomena.
senses.exampleCN: criterion/criteria 遵循希腊语模式，就像 phenomenon/phenomena。
senses.why: The -a ending is not an English plural but a Greek one carried over. Once you see the pattern, criteria, phenomena and automata stop looking irregular.
senses.whyCN: -a 词尾不是英语复数，而是被保留下来的希腊语复数。看懂这个模式后，criteria、phenomena、automata 就不再显得不规则。

intro.en: Criteria is not an English plural made with -s; it is the Greek plural of criterion. The singular ends in -on, the plural in -a, and both come from krinein 'to separate, decide'.
intro.cn: criteria 不是用 -s 构成的英语复数，而是 criterion 的希腊语复数。单数结尾 -on，复数结尾 -a，两者都来自 krinein“分开、判定”。

items.en: criterion is first recorded in English meaning 'a standard for judging'. The Greek plural criteria came with it.
items.cn: criterion 于 17 世纪 20 年代最早进入英语，意为“判断的标准”；希腊语复数 criteria 随之进入。

items.en: From Greek kritērion 'means for judging, standard', from kritēs 'judge', from krinein 'to separate, decide'.
items.cn: 来自希腊语 kritērion“判断的工具、标准”，出自 kritēs“法官”，再上溯 krinein“分开、判定”。

items.en: kriterion is a neuter noun in -on; Greek neuters of this class form the plural in -a. Hence kriterion → kritēria, with no -s.
items.cn: kriterion 是以 -on 结尾的中性名词；这类希腊中性名词复数用 -a。因此 kriterion → kritēria，不加 -s。

items.en: krinein is traced to PIE *krei- 'to sieve, discriminate, distinguish', also behind crisis and critic. The reconstruction is generally accepted.
items.cn: krinein 被追溯到原始印欧语 *krei-“筛、区分、辨别”，crisis 和 critic 也出自这里。该重构属于一般认为是。

items.en: English uses criteria as the plural; in the 20c. 'a criteria' spreads in informal writing even though the singular is criterion.
items.cn: 英语用 criteria 作复数；20 世纪“a criteria”在非正式写作中扩散，尽管单数形式是 criterion。

items.en: Modern technical usage fixes phrases such as diagnostic criteria, selection criteria and acceptance criteria, where the plural is almost always required.
items.cn: 现代技术用法固定了 diagnostic criteria、selection criteria、acceptance criteria 等短语，这些短语几乎总用复数。

note.en: The first group shares krinein 'separate, decide'; the second group separates standards, benchmarks, measuring tools and plain rules.
note.cn: 第一组共享 krinein“分开、判定”；第二组区分标准、基准、测量工具和普通规则。

entries.definition: one standard for judging. It is the singular that criteria replaces in the plural.
entries.definitionCN: 一条判断标准。它就是 criteria 在复数中替换掉的单数形式。

entries.definition: decisive, or involving judgement and criticism. It shares krinein 'decide'.
entries.definitionCN: 关键的，或涉及判断与批评的。它共享 krinein“判定”。

entries.definition: a turning point that demands a decision. Greek krisis meant 'a separating, a decision'.
entries.definitionCN: 需要作出决定的转折点。希腊语 krisis 意为“分离、判定”。

entries.definition: a level of quality or a rule used for comparison. It is broader and can be singular or plural.
entries.definitionCN: 用于比较的质量水平或规则。它更宽泛，可单数也可复数。

entries.definition: a known reference point against which performance is measured. It is usually one point, not a set.
entries.definitionCN: 用来衡量表现的已知参照点。它通常是一个点，不是一套。

entries.definition: an instrument or a standard for measuring. It stresses measurement more than judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 测量仪器或衡量标准。它更强调测量，而不是判断。

entries.definition: a standard used to compare quality or success. It is informal and often singular.
entries.definitionCN: 用来比较质量或成功的标准。它偏口语，常作单数。

normalIntro.en: Real morphology: Greek krinein 'separate, decide' gives criterion, criteria, critic, critical and crisis. The -on/-a plural is a Greek pattern, not an English one.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词：希腊语 krinein“分开、判定”给出 criterion、criteria、critic、critical、crisis。-on/-a 复数是希腊语模式，不是英语模式。

normal.en: One criterion, two criteria. If you remember the Greek -on/-a pair, you will never write 'a criteria'.
normal.cn: 一个 criterion，两个 criteria。记住希腊语 -on/-a 这一对，就不会写出 a criteria。

normal.en: Criterion, critic, critical and crisis all contain krinein 'separate, decide'. A criterion is the tool that separates.
normal.cn: criterion、critic、critical、crisis 都含 krinein“分开、判定”。criterion 就是那把用来分开的工具。

normal.en: Selection criteria are the sieve holes: change the holes, and a different group passes through.
normal.cn: 选拔标准就是筛子的孔：换掉孔径，通过的群体就变了。

normal.en: Diagnostic criteria decide a case before treatment begins, just as a judge decides before sentence.
normal.cn: 诊断标准在治疗开始前就决定了病例，就像法官在量刑前先判定。

normal.en: Acceptance criteria are written before the work starts, so 'done' is defined in advance.
normal.cn: 验收标准在开工前就写好，所以“完成”是被预先定义的。

abstract.en: Picture a sieve held over a pile of applicants. The holes are the criteria; the sieve does not argue with anyone.
abstract.cn: 想象一把筛子悬在一堆申请者上方。孔就是标准；筛子不跟任何人争论。

abstract.en: A criterion is a ruler laid against a thing. Remove the ruler, and 'better' and 'worse' become opinions again.
abstract.cn: criterion 是贴在某物上的一把尺。拿掉尺子，“更好”和“更差”就又变回意见。

abstract.en: The Greek plural -a is a fossil: the word still carries the shape of the language that made it.
abstract.cn: 希腊语复数 -a 是一块化石：这个词仍带着制造它的那种语言的形状。

examples.en: The panel listed the criteria before reading any application.
examples.cn: 评审组在阅读任何申请之前先列出了标准。

examples.en: No single criterion can capture teaching quality.
examples.cn: 没有任何单一标准能完全衡量教学质量。

examples.en: The new criteria take effect next semester.
examples.cn: 新标准下学期生效。

dict_mnemonic.text: “克瑞特里亚”——克瑞特里亚拿尺子把候选人分成合格与不合格 → criteria 标准（criterion 的复数）

root: 希腊语 kritērion“判断的依据”，来自 krinein“分开、判定”，核心是“用来筛分好坏的那把尺”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of criteria, all one act of judging: standards in general, the plural rule, selection, diagnosis, design, eligibility, acceptance, research, and the Greek -on/-a pattern that explains the form.
sensesIntro.cn: criteria 的九个义项都是同一个“判定”：一般标准、复数规则、选拔、诊断、设计、资格、验收、研究，以及解释其词形的希腊语 -on/-a 模式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sieve whose holes decide what passes through.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把筛子，孔的大小决定谁能通过。

branches.en: FORM: the plural means more than one standard, and the Greek -a ending explains why.
branches.cn: 形式：复数表示不止一条标准，希腊语 -a 词尾解释了这个形式。

branches.en: ADMISSION: selection and eligibility criteria decide who is let in.
branches.cn: 准入：选拔与资格标准决定谁被放进来。

branches.en: EVIDENCE: diagnosis and research criteria decide what counts as a valid case.
branches.cn: 证据：诊断与研究标准决定什么算有效案例。

branches.en: PRODUCTION: design and acceptance criteria decide whether work passes.
branches.cn: 生产：设计与验收标准决定工作是否通过。

branches.en: MORPHOLOGY: the Greek neuter pattern keeps the plural separate from English -s.
branches.cn: 词形：希腊中性名词模式使这个复数不走英语 -s。

intro.en: criteria has no live English affixes. Its ending is a Greek plural, and its relatives are separate borrowings from the same krinein family.
intro.cn: criteria 没有活的英语词缀。它的词尾是希腊语复数，同族词是从同一个 krinein 词族分别借入的。

latinIntro.en: The family comes from Greek, not Latin: krinein 'separate, decide' gives critic, critical, criticism, crisis and criterion.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族来自希腊语而非拉丁语：krinein“分开、判定”给出 critic、critical、criticism、crisis、criterion。

items.meaning: one standard for judging
items.meaningCN: 单数形式：一条判断标准
items.example: Cost is only one criterion among several.
items.exampleCN: 成本只是若干标准中的一条。

items.meaning: decisive, or involving judgement and analysis
items.meaningCN: 关键的；批判性的（能够判断）
items.example: Critical thinking compares evidence before deciding.
items.exampleCN: 批判性思维在决定前先比较证据。

items.meaning: a person who judges and comments on works
items.meaningCN: 批评家；评论者（作出判断的人）
items.example: The critic praised the film's restraint.
items.exampleCN: 评论者称赞了影片的克制。

items.meaning: a turning point that demands a decision
items.meaningCN: 危机；转折点（必须作出决定的时刻）
items.example: The shortage became a crisis by midwinter.
items.exampleCN: 短缺在隆冬时演变成危机。

items.meaning: the work of judging faults, or a considered judgment
items.meaningCN: 批评；评论（-ism 表示活动或论说）
items.example: The essay drew sharp criticism.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章招来尖锐的批评。

items.meaning: to judge or point out faults
items.meaningCN: 批评；评判（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The report criticizes the design.
items.exampleCN: 报告批评了这项设计。

items.meaning: a detailed judgment of a work
items.meaningCN: 评论；评析（源自希腊语 kritikē“评判术”）
items.example: She wrote a critique of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 她写了一篇对该计划的评析。

items.meaning: in a judging way, or crucially
items.meaningCN: 批判性地；关键地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: He read the draft critically.
items.exampleCN: 他批判性地读了这份草稿。

latinEntries.meaning: to judge and point out faults
latinEntries.meaningCN: 批评；指出缺点（作出判断）

latinEntries.meaning: a detailed judgement of a work
latinEntries.meaningCN: 评论；批评文章（对作品的详细判断）

latinEntries.meaning: too ready to find faults
latinEntries.meaningCN: 吹毛求疵的（过度批判）

latinEntries.meaning: pretending to have beliefs one does not hold
latinEntries.meaningCN: 虚伪（希腊语“演戏、扮演”，与 krinein 同一语源群）

definition_zh: 关键的；决定性的；至关重要的；十字形的（旧义）
definition_en: extremely important because it decides what happens; literally, cross-shaped
core_image: 十字路口的那根路标：往左还是往右，全看它
scene: 战术板上圈出最后一攻的箭头，球员围着教练。 The coach circled the last attack on the tactics board and called it the crucial moment of the match.
sceneCN: 这里 crucial 是「决定性的、关键的」（第 1 个义项：决定结果的关键时刻）；句意：教练在战术板上圈出最后一攻，称这是比赛的关键时刻。

pos.zh: 关键的；决定性的；十字形的（旧义）

senses.title: Decisive for the outcome
senses.definition: so important that it decides which way a situation will end
senses.definitionCN: 重要到足以决定局势最终走向
senses.example: The next vote is crucial for the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 下一次投票对这项法案至关重要。
senses.why: crucial comes from Latin crux 'cross'. The decisive sense is generally considered to be from the image of a cross standing at a fork: one road leads to one future, the other to another.
senses.whyCN: crucial 来自拉丁语 crux“十字”。决定性义一般认为是来自十字路口立着十字架的意象：一条路通向一种未来，另一条通向另一种。

senses.title: Extremely important
senses.definition: needed for something to succeed; essential
senses.definitionCN: 某事成功所必需；必不可少
senses.example: Sleep is crucial to memory.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠对记忆至关重要。
senses.why: The weaker everyday sense keeps the decision point but drops the drama. Without this factor, the outcome fails, so it is still the hinge of the situation.
senses.whyCN: 较弱的日常义保留了“决定点”，但少了戏剧性。没有这个因素，结果就会失败，所以它仍是局势的铰链。

senses.title: Cross-shaped
senses.definition: in technical or older usage, shaped like a cross
senses.definitionCN: 在技术或较旧用法中，形状像十字
senses.example: A crucial incision crosses the lesion.
senses.exampleCN: 十字形切口横跨病灶。
senses.why: This is the oldest recorded sense, from Latin crux 'cross'. English first used crucial for anything cross-shaped before it used it for decisive moments.
senses.whyCN: 这是最早记录的义项，来自拉丁语 crux“十字”。英语先用 crucial 指任何十字形的东西，之后才用于决定性的时刻。

senses.title: Anatomy: the cruciate ligament
senses.definition: in anatomy, a ligament that crosses another, especially the cruciate ligaments of the knee
senses.definitionCN: 解剖学中与另一条韧带交叉的韧带，尤指膝十字韧带
senses.example: The cruciate ligaments cross inside the knee, a crucial detail for surgeons.
senses.exampleCN: 十字韧带在膝关节内交叉，这对骨科医生来说是关键细节。
senses.why: The ligament literally crosses the joint, forming a cross with its partner. Older English also called it the crucial ligament, which shows the cross sense surviving in medicine.
senses.whyCN: 这条韧带字面上横跨关节，与伙伴形成十字。较早的英语也称它为 crucial ligament，可见“十字”义在医学中保留下来。

senses.title: Crucial experiment
senses.definition: a scientific test that decides between two competing hypotheses
senses.definitionCN: 在两条竞争假说之间作出裁决的科学实验
senses.example: The crucial experiment ruled out the rival theory.
senses.exampleCN: 这个判决性实验排除了竞争理论。
senses.why: Francis Bacon's phrase experimentum crucis, 'experiment of the cross', pictured a crossroads where a hypothesis must take one road. This is the bridge from 'cross' to 'decisive'.
senses.whyCN: 弗朗西斯·培根的 experimentum crucis（“十字实验”）把实验想象成岔路口：假说必须选择一条路。这就是从“十字”走向“决定性”的桥梁。

senses.title: At the crucial moment
senses.definition: at the single point in time when the outcome is decided
senses.definitionCN: 结果被决定的那个时间点
senses.example: At the crucial moment, the goalkeeper guessed right.
senses.exampleCN: 在关键时刻，守门员猜对了方向。
senses.why: The crossroads is now in time: one instant separates two futures. The word marks the instant when the two roads diverge.
senses.whyCN: 岔路口此时在时间上：一个瞬间分开两种未来。这个词标记两条路分开的那一刻。

senses.title: The crux of the matter
senses.definition: in the related noun crux, the central and decisive point of an argument or problem
senses.definitionCN: 相关名词 crux 表示论证或问题中最中心、最具决定性的点
senses.example: The crux of the dispute is money, and that is the crucial point.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争论的关键是钱，而这就是那个决定性的要点。
senses.why: crux is the Latin word for cross, and a crux is the point where everything turns. The noun makes the fork image visible as the 'crossing point' of an argument.
senses.whyCN: crux 就是拉丁语“十字”，而症结就是一切转折的那个点。这个名词把岔路意象显现为论证的“交叉点”。

senses.title: Crucially: as a decisive point
senses.definition: in the adverb crucially, used to mark the point on which the rest depends
senses.definitionCN: 副词 crucially 用于标记其余一切所依赖的那一点
senses.example: Crucially, the sample was collected before dawn, a crucial detail for dating it.
senses.exampleCN: 关键在于，样本在天亮前采集，这对测定年代十分重要。
senses.why: The adverb flags the hinge of an explanation. It tells the reader: if you miss this point, the rest will not follow.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词标记解释的铰链。它告诉读者：漏掉这一点，其余就推不出来。

intro.en: Crucial began as a shape word: Latin crux 'cross'. The 'decisive' sense is generally traced to the cross at a fork in the road, and to Bacon's experimentum crucis.
intro.cn: crucial 最初是一个形状词：拉丁语 crux“十字”。它的“决定性”义一般追溯到岔路口的十字标志，以及培根的 experimentum crucis。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'cross-shaped', from French crucial and Latin crux 'cross'.
items.cn: 17 世纪 40 年代最早记录，意为“十字形的”，来自法语 crucial 和拉丁语 crux“十字”。

items.en: crux (genitive crucis) meant 'cross, gallows, torment'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain in standard references.
items.cn: crux（属格 crucis）意为“十字、十字架、刑具”。它更深层的来源在通行资料中属于来源不确定。

items.en: Bacon's experimentum crucis, 'experiment of the cross', named a test that decides between rival explanations. The phrase is the usual bridge to the modern sense.
items.cn: 培根的 experimentum crucis（“十字实验”）指在竞争解释之间作出裁决的实验。这个说法通常被视为通往现代义的桥梁。

items.en: The sense 'decisive' is recorded from the 1830s. It is generally considered to be built on the image of a cross standing where two roads divide.
items.cn: “决定性的”义见于 19 世纪 30 年代。它一般认为是建立在“十字立在两条路分开处”的意象上。

items.en: Crucial ligament becomes cruciate ligament in anatomy; crucial experiment and crucial moment become standard academic and journalistic phrases.
items.cn: 解剖学中 crucial ligament 演变为 cruciate ligament；crucial experiment 与 crucial moment 成为标准的学术和新闻短语。

items.en: Modern English uses crucial mainly for importance. Crux, cruciform, crucify and crusade keep the literal cross, so the family still shows the original shape.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用 crucial 表示重要性。crux、cruciform、crucify、crusade 保留字面上的十字，因此词族仍显示最初形状。

note.en: The first group shares crux 'cross'; the second group separates decisive, critical, vital and pivotal kinds of importance.
note.cn: 第一组共享 crux“十字”；第二组区分决定性的、关键性的、生命攸关的和枢纽性的重要性。

entries.definition: the decisive point of a problem, literally a cross. It is the noun behind crucial.
entries.definitionCN: 问题的症结，字面义“十字”。它是 crucial 背后的名词。

entries.definition: shaped like a cross. It preserves the oldest literal sense of crucial.
entries.definitionCN: 十字形的。它保留了 crucial 最古老的字面义。

entries.definition: crossed, used of knee ligaments. It shows the medical branch of the cross image.
entries.definitionCN: 交叉的，用于膝韧带。它展示了十字意象的医学分支。

entries.definition: extremely important, especially at a point where a judgement decides. It overlaps crucial but also means 'fault-finding'.
entries.definitionCN: 极其重要，尤指在某判断点上。它与 crucial 重叠，但也有“吹毛求疵”义。

entries.definition: able to settle a result or question. It is more explicit than crucial about the act of deciding.
entries.definitionCN: 能够决定结果或问题的。它比 crucial 更明确地指向“作出决定”。

entries.definition: absolutely necessary for life or success. It stresses necessity, not a fork in the road.
entries.definitionCN: 生命或成功绝对必需的。它强调必要性，而不是岔路口。

entries.definition: central and decisive, like a hinge on which something turns. It is close to crucial but more spatial.
entries.definitionCN: 中心且决定性的，像物体转动的铰链。它接近 crucial，但更偏空间意象。

normalIntro.en: Real family: Latin crux 'cross' gives crucial, crux, cruciform, crucify and crusade. The decisive sense is generally traced through the cross at a fork and Bacon's experimentum crucis.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词族：拉丁语 crux“十字”给出 crucial、crux、cruciform、crucify、crusade。决定性义一般追溯到岔路口的十字和培根的 experimentum crucis。

normal.en: crux means cross. A crucial decision is the cross where two roads part: you cannot take both.
normal.cn: crux 意为十字。crucial decision 就是两条路分开的十字处：你不能两条都走。

normal.en: crucify, crusade and cruciform all keep the literal cross, which is why the family still looks like a shape word.
normal.cn: crucify、crusade、cruciform 都保留字面上的十字，所以这个词族看起来仍像一个形状词。

normal.en: A crucial experiment is one that forces a theory to take one road and abandon the other.
normal.cn: crucial experiment 就是逼一个理论选择一条路、放弃另一条路的实验。

normal.en: The crux of the matter is the crossing point where the argument turns.
normal.cn: “the crux of the matter”就是论证转向的那个交叉点。

normal.en: Crucially marks the hinge of an explanation: miss it, and the rest will not follow.
normal.cn: crucially 标记解释的铰链：漏掉它，其余就推不出来。

abstract.en: A signpost at a fork: two arrows, one pole. The pole does not choose, but it is where the choice becomes visible.
abstract.cn: 岔路口的一块路标：两个箭头，一根杆。杆不选择，但选择在那里变得可见。

abstract.en: A hinge does not move the door by itself; it only makes the door able to turn. Crucial things are hinges.
abstract.cn: 铰链本身不推门，只是让门能够转动。关键事物就是铰链。

abstract.en: One domino in a long chain looks small, yet every later domino depends on whether it falls.
abstract.cn: 长链中的一块多米诺骨牌看起来很小，但后面每一块都取决于它倒不倒。

examples.en: The first two years are crucial for language development.
examples.cn: 前两年对语言发展至关重要。

examples.en: Crucially, the team tested the sample twice.
examples.cn: 关键的是，团队对样本做了两次测试。

examples.en: The crux of the case is whether the contract was signed.
examples.cn: 案件的关键在于合同是否签署。

dict_mnemonic.text: “克鲁舍”——克鲁舍在十字路口立了块牌子，指明朝哪边走 → crucial 关键的、决定性的

root: 拉丁语 crux“十字、十字路口”，核心是“岔路口那个决定方向的位置”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of crucial, all one crossroad: the decisive vote, plain importance, the literal cross shape, the crossing ligament, the deciding experiment, the decisive instant, the crux, and the adverb that marks the hinge.
sensesIntro.cn: crucial 的八个义项都是同一个岔路口：决定性的投票、日常的重要性、字面上的十字形、交叉的韧带、作出裁决的实验、决定性的瞬间、症结，以及标记铰链的副词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cross stands at the fork where two futures divide.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个十字立在两条未来分开的岔口。

branches.en: DECISION: the vote, the important factor and the decisive instant all sit at the fork.
branches.cn: 决定：投票、重要因素、决定性瞬间都位于岔口。

branches.en: SHAPE: the literal cross survives in technical and anatomical usage.
branches.cn: 形状：字面上的十字保留在技术与解剖用法里。

branches.en: SCIENCE: the crucial experiment forces one hypothesis to take one road.
branches.cn: 科学：判决性实验逼一条假说选择一条路。

branches.en: CRUX: the crossing point of an argument is its decisive knot.
branches.cn: 症结：论证的交叉点就是它决定性的结。

branches.en: ADVERB: crucially points to the hinge on which the rest turns.
branches.cn: 副词：crucially 指向其余部分所转动的铰链。

intro.en: crucial takes -ly for the adverb, while the root crux also gives the noun crux and the technical compounds cruciform and cruciate.
intro.cn: crucial 加 -ly 构成副词；词根 crux 还给出名词 crux，以及技术复合词 cruciform、cruciate。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on crux 'cross': crux, crucify, cruciform, crusade and cruciate all show a literal or historical cross.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 crux“十字”上：crux、crucify、cruciform、crusade、cruciate 都显示字面或历史上的十字。

items.meaning: in a way that marks the decisive point
items.meaningCN: 关键地；至关重要地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Crucially, no one had checked the second door.
items.exampleCN: 关键的是，没有人检查过第二扇门。

items.meaning: the central, decisive point of a problem
items.meaningCN: 症结；关键（问题最中心的决定点）
items.example: The crux is whether the data can be trusted.
items.exampleCN: 关键在于这些数据是否可信。

items.meaning: shaped like a cross
items.meaningCN: 十字形的（-form 表示形状）
items.example: The church has a cruciform plan.
items.exampleCN: 这座教堂是十字形平面。

items.structure: Old French croisade, from Latin crux (cross)
items.meaning: a religious war or a determined campaign for a cause
items.meaningCN: 十字军东征；为某项事业发起的运动（源自“十字”）
items.example: She led a crusade against plastic waste.
items.exampleCN: 她发起了一场反对塑料垃圾的运动。

items.meaning: to put to death on a cross, or to torment
items.meaningCN: 钉死在十字架上；严厉折磨（-ify 表示使成为）
items.example: Critics crucified the first draft.
items.exampleCN: 批评者把初稿批得体无完肤。

items.meaning: cross-shaped, as of certain ligaments
items.meaningCN: 十字形的（-ate 表形状，用于韧带等）
items.example: He tore a cruciate ligament.
items.exampleCN: 他撕裂了一条十字韧带。

items.meaning: a cross with the figure of Christ on it
items.meaningCN: 十字架苦像（-fix 表示固定）
items.example: A small crucifix hung above the door.
items.exampleCN: 门上方挂着一枚小十字架。

items.meaning: extremely painful
items.meaningCN: 极痛苦的；难以忍受的（由 crux“十字”派生的折磨义）
items.example: The wait was excruciating.
items.exampleCN: 等待令人难以忍受。

latinEntries.meaning: to put to death on a cross; to torment
latinEntries.meaningCN: 钉死在十字架上；折磨（固定在十字上）

latinEntries.meaning: a cross with a figure of Christ
latinEntries.meaningCN: 十字苦像（带基督像的十字架）

latinEntries.meaning: crossed, shaped like a cross
latinEntries.meaningCN: 交叉的；十字形的

latinEntries.meaning: extremely painful, literally 'out of the cross'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 极度痛苦的（字面义“出自十字架”）

definition_zh: 文化；文明；养殖；培养物；耕种（旧义）
definition_en: the customs, arts, and way of life of a group; the growing of cells or microorganisms in a prepared medium
core_image: 一块被反复耕种的田：种什么、怎么种，决定长出什么
scene: 展柜里摆着民族服饰、乐器与节日照片。 At the display case the children looked at clothes, instruments, and festival photos from a different culture.
sceneCN: 这里 culture 是「文化」（第 1 个义项：一个群体的生活方式与习俗）；句意：在展柜前，孩子们观看另一种文化的服饰、乐器和节日照片。

senses.title: The way of life of a people
senses.definition: the customs, beliefs, food, language, and arts that a group of people share
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体共享的习俗、信念、饮食、语言与艺术
senses.example: Food is a central part of every culture.
senses.exampleCN: 饮食是每种文化的核心部分。
senses.why: Latin cultura meant 'cultivation', from colere 'to till, tend, care'. A way of life is what a society tends and passes on, generation after generation, like a field kept in use.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cultura 意为“耕种”，来自 colere“耕作、照料、关心”。生活方式就是一个社会一代代照料、传递的东西，像一块持续耕种的田。

senses.title: The arts and intellectual life
senses.definition: the arts, literature, music, and refined intellectual activity of a society
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会的艺术、文学、音乐与精致的精神活动
senses.example: She studies literature and culture.
senses.exampleCN: 她研究文学与文化。
senses.why: The cultivated field becomes the cultivated mind. High culture is what a society has deliberately grown and refined, not just what it happens to do.
senses.whyCN: 被耕种的田变成了被教养的心灵。高雅文化是一个社会有意培育、精致化的东西，而不只是它碰巧在做的事。

senses.title: Shared habits of an organisation
senses.definition: the accepted values, habits, and ways of behaving inside a company or group
senses.definitionCN: 公司或群体内部被接受的价值、习惯与行为方式
senses.example: The company's culture rewards candor.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的文化鼓励直言。
senses.why: The cultivation metaphor moves indoors: a group's habits are grown by repeated practice, and new members are planted into that soil.
senses.whyCN: 耕种比喻移到室内：一个群体的习惯通过反复实践被培养出来，新成员则被种进那片土壤。

senses.title: Growing crops: the oldest sense
senses.definition: the preparation and tending of land for crops; agriculture
senses.definitionCN: 为种植作物而整地、照料土地；农业
senses.example: The culture of wheat shaped early settlements.
senses.exampleCN: 小麦的种植塑造了早期定居点。
senses.why: This is the literal source: cultura is the act of tilling and tending. Everything abstract in the word grows out of this physical labour.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面源头：cultura 就是耕作与照料的行为。这个词里所有抽象含义都是从这种体力劳动中长出来的。

senses.title: Growing microorganisms in a lab
senses.definition: the controlled growing of bacteria, cells, or tissue in a prepared nutrient medium
senses.definitionCN: 在配好的营养基质中受控地培养细菌、细胞或组织
senses.example: The lab prepared a bacterial culture.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室准备了细菌培养物。
senses.why: 19c microbiology borrowed the farming image: microbes are 'planted' in a medium and 'grown'. The technique keeps the original agricultural verb.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪微生物学借用了农耕意象：微生物被“种”进培养基并被“养大”。这项技术保留了最初的农业动词。

senses.title: The growth itself
senses.definition: the population of cells or microorganisms that has been grown
senses.definitionCN: 被培养出来的那一片细胞或微生物群体
senses.example: The culture turned cloudy overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 培养物一夜之间变浑了。
senses.why: The noun shifts from the act to the thing produced, just as 'a planting' can mean the crop rather than the work. The field image now names what grew in it.
senses.whyCN: 名词从行为转向产物，正如“种植”也可以指长出来的庄稼而不是劳作。田地意象此时命名的是田里长出的东西。

senses.title: Cultured: refined or artificially grown
senses.definition: in the adjective cultured, refined by education, or grown in a controlled medium
senses.definitionCN: 形容词 cultured 表示经教育熏陶的，或在受控基质中培养的
senses.example: A cultured pearl is grown in an oyster.
senses.exampleCN: 养殖珍珠是在牡蛎中培育出来的。
senses.why: The participle covers both branches of cultivation: a person can be 'grown' by education, and a pearl can be 'grown' in an oyster. Both are tended, not wild.
senses.whyCN: 分词覆盖耕种的两条分支：人可以经教育被“养成”，珍珠可以在牡蛎里被“养出”。两者都是被照料的，而非野生的。

senses.title: Cultural: belonging to a way of life
senses.titleCN: 文化的：属于某种生活方式
senses.definition: in the adjective cultural, relating to the customs, arts, or beliefs of a group
senses.definitionCN: 形容词 cultural 表示与群体的习俗、艺术或信念有关
senses.example: Cultural differences affect negotiation, and negotiators who ignore culture lose deals.
senses.exampleCN: 文化差异会影响谈判，忽视文化的谈判者会丢掉生意。
senses.why: The adjective marks anything that belongs to the cultivated life of a group. It is the most neutral and general form of the whole family.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记属于某个群体“被耕种的生活”的一切。它是整个词族中最中性、最一般的形式。

senses.title: To culture cells
senses.definition: to grow cells, bacteria, or tissue in a controlled medium
senses.definitionCN: 在受控基质中培养细胞、细菌或组织
senses.example: Researchers culture skin cells for grafts.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员培养皮肤细胞用于移植。
senses.why: The verb returns to the literal act of tending and growing. What was a metaphor in sense 1 is here a laboratory procedure.
senses.whyCN: 动词回到字面上的照料与生长行为。在第 1 个义项里是比喻的东西，在这里是实验室操作。

intro.en: Culture is a farming word before it is an art word. Latin cultura 'tilling' comes from colere 'to tend, cultivate, also to worship'. The mind and the arts were later described as things that could be cultivated.
intro.cn: culture 先是一个农耕词，然后才是艺术词。拉丁语 cultura“耕种”来自 colere“照料、耕作，也有敬奉之义”。后来，心灵与艺术也被描述为可以被“耕种”的东西。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'cultivation of land, tillage'. The figurative sense 'training of the mind' follows in the 16c.
items.cn: 15 世纪中期最早记录，意为“耕种土地”；“心灵的培养”这一比喻义随后在 16 世纪出现。

items.en: From Latin cultura 'a cultivating, agriculture', figuratively 'care, culture, an honoring', from colere 'to tend, guard, cultivate, till'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 cultura“耕种、农业”，比喻义为“照料、修养、敬奉”，出自 colere“照料、守护、耕作”。

items.en: colere also meant 'to worship', which gives cult and cultivate. The same verb covers tilling soil, tending a god, and training a mind.
items.cn: colere 也有“敬奉”义，由此产生 cult 和 cultivate。同一个动词覆盖翻土、敬神和培养心灵。

items.en: colere is traced to PIE *kwel- (1) 'to turn around, sojourn, dwell'. The reconstruction is generally accepted.
items.cn: colere 被追溯到原始印欧语 *kwel-（第 1 义）“转动、停留、居住”。该重构属于一般认为是。

items.en: Culture becomes the name of the arts and refined taste, then of a whole society's way of life. Tylor's anthropological definition appears in 1871.
items.cn: culture 在 18—19 世纪成为艺术与精致品味的名称，再成为一个社会整体生活方式的名称。泰勒的人类学定义出现于 1871 年。

items.en: Bacteriology borrows culture for growing microbes (1880s); corporate culture and culture shock become common in the 20c.
items.cn: 细菌学在 19 世纪 80 年代借用 culture 表示培养微生物；corporate culture 与 culture shock 在 20 世纪普及。

note.en: The first group shares colere 'tend'; the second group separates civilisation, customs, society and personal refinement.
note.cn: 第一组共享 colere“照料”；第二组区分文明、习俗、社会和个人修养。

entries.definition: to prepare land, grow crops, or develop a quality. It is the verb behind culture.
entries.definitionCN: 整地、种植，或培养某种品质。它就是 culture 背后的动词。

entries.definition: a system of worship or a small devoted group. It comes from colere 'worship'.
entries.definitionCN: 崇拜体系，或一个小型狂热团体。它来自 colere“敬奉”。

entries.definition: farming: ager 'field' + cultura 'cultivation'. The word makes the farming sense visible.
entries.definitionCN: 农业：ager“田地”+ cultura“耕种”。这个词让耕种义变得可见。

entries.definition: an advanced society with cities, laws, and technology. It is broader and more structural than culture.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有城市、法律和技术的发达社会。它比 culture 更宽泛、更重结构。

entries.definition: the traditional practices of a group. It is narrower than culture and names behaviours rather than the whole way of life.
entries.definitionCN: 群体的传统做法。它比 culture 窄，命名的是行为而非整体生活方式。

entries.definition: the people of a community and their organised relations. It is the group itself, while culture is its learned way of life.
entries.definitionCN: 一个共同体的人及其组织关系。它是群体本身，而 culture 是群体习得的生活方式。

entries.definition: the quality of being educated and polished. It matches the 'cultured person' branch, not culture as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 有教养、精致的气质。它对应“有教养的人”这一支，而不是整体的文化。

normalIntro.en: Real family: Latin colere 'till, tend, worship' gives culture, cultivate, cult and agriculture. The farming image is the root of all the abstract senses.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词族：拉丁语 colere“耕种、照料、敬奉”给出 culture、cultivate、cult、agriculture。农耕意象是所有抽象义的根。

normal.en: cultura means tilling. A culture is a way of life that has been tended over generations, like a field kept fertile.
normal.cn: cultura 意为耕种。文化就是一种被一代代照料的生活方式，像一块保持肥沃的田。

normal.en: Cultivate, cult and agriculture all come from colere: to grow crops, to worship, and to farm a field.
normal.cn: cultivate、cult、agriculture 都来自 colere：种庄稼、敬奉、耕田。

normal.en: A laboratory culture is a tiny farm: microbes are planted in a medium and grown.
normal.cn: 实验室的 culture 是一块微型农田：微生物被种进培养基并养大。

normal.en: Corporate culture is the soil new employees are planted into.
normal.cn: 企业文化就是新员工被种进去的那片土壤。

normal.en: A cultured pearl is not wild; it is grown under control, just as a cultured person is shaped by education.
normal.cn: 养殖珍珠不是野生的，而是在控制下养出来的；有教养的人也一样，是被教育塑造的。

abstract.en: Picture a field that has been worked for a thousand years. The soil, the walls, and the paths all remember the work.
abstract.cn: 想象一块被耕作了一千年的田。土壤、田埂和路径都记得那些劳作。

abstract.en: A petri dish is a field seen through glass: the same planting, the same tending, only much smaller.
abstract.cn: 培养皿就是隔着玻璃看见的一块田：同样的播种、同样的照料，只是小得多。

abstract.en: A theatre stage is where a society shows itself what it has grown to value.
abstract.cn: 剧场舞台是一个社会向自己展示“它养成了什么价值”的地方。

examples.en: The museum presents the cultures of five river valleys.
examples.cn: 博物馆展示了五个河谷地区的文化。

examples.en: The lab cultures bacteria at body temperature.
examples.cn: 实验室在体温条件下培养细菌。

examples.en: A strong safety culture prevents small errors from becoming disasters.
examples.cn: 强大的安全文化能防止小错误变成灾难。

dict_mnemonic.text: “考尔扯”——靠着一代代耕作与教养，才长出一种文化 → culture 文化、培养

root: 拉丁语 colere“耕作、照料、敬奉”，名词 cultura 本义“耕种”，核心是“被一代代照料、培育出来的生活方式”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of culture, all one field being tended: a way of life, the arts, an organisation's habits, crops, microbes, the growth itself, the cultured adjective, the cultural adjective, and the verb 'to grow'.
sensesIntro.cn: culture 的九个义项都是同一块被照料的田：生活方式、艺术、组织风气、庄稼、微生物、培养物本身、cultured 形容词、cultural 形容词，以及动词“培养”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field is tilled, planted, and tended until something grows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块田被翻耕、播种、照料，最后长出东西。

branches.en: SOCIETY: a shared way of life and its cultivated arts.
branches.cn: 社会：共享的生活方式及其被培育的艺术。

branches.en: ORGANISATION: a group's habits are grown by repeated practice.
branches.cn: 组织：群体的习惯通过反复实践被养成。

branches.en: FARMING: the literal sense survives in crops and in the verb 'to culture'.
branches.cn: 农耕：字面义保留在庄稼和动词“培养”里。

branches.en: LABORATORY: microbes are planted and grown; the growth itself is also called a culture.
branches.cn: 实验室：微生物被种下并养大；长出来的东西也叫 culture。

branches.en: ADJECTIVES: cultured marks refinement or controlled growth; cultural marks belonging to a way of life.
branches.cn: 形容词：cultured 标记教养或受控培养；cultural 标记属于某种生活方式。

intro.en: culture takes -al for the adjective, -ally for the adverb, and -ed for the participle. Agriculture shows the same cultura joined to ager 'field'.
intro.cn: culture 加 -al 构成形容词，加 -ally 构成副词，加 -ed 构成分词。agriculture 显示同一个 cultura 与 ager“田地”结合。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on colere 'till, tend, worship': cultivate, cult, agriculture, horticulture and culture itself all describe tending something until it grows.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 colere“耕种、照料、敬奉”上：cultivate、cult、agriculture、horticulture、culture 都描述照料某物直到它长成。

items.meaning: relating to the customs, arts, or beliefs of a group
items.meaningCN: 文化的（-al 表示“与……有关”）
items.example: The festival is a cultural event, not a commercial one.
items.exampleCN: 这个节日是文化活动，不是商业活动。

items.meaning: in cultural terms
items.meaningCN: 在文化层面上（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two regions are culturally close.
items.exampleCN: 这两个地区在文化上很接近。

items.meaning: refined by education; grown in a controlled medium
items.meaningCN: 有教养的；人工培养的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: Cultured cells grow evenly in the dish.
items.exampleCN: 培养细胞在皿中均匀生长。

items.meaning: the practice of farming
items.meaningCN: 农业（田地＋耕种）
items.example: Agriculture changed the river valley within a century.
items.exampleCN: 农业在一个世纪内改变了这条河谷。

items.meaning: to prepare land for crops, or to foster growth
items.meaningCN: 耕种；培养（与 colere“耕作”同根）
items.example: They cultivate rice on the lower terraces.
items.exampleCN: 他们在较低的梯田上种稻。

items.meaning: the act of tilling or fostering
items.meaningCN: 耕作；培养（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: Cultivation began in the river valley.
items.exampleCN: 耕作始于河谷。

items.meaning: the art of growing garden plants
items.meaningCN: 园艺（hortus“园圃”+ cultura“耕作”）
items.example: She studied horticulture in college.
items.exampleCN: 她在大学学的是园艺。

items.meaning: a group with its own norms inside a larger culture
items.meaningCN: 亚文化（sub- 表在……之内）
items.example: Skateboarding has its own subculture.
items.exampleCN: 滑板运动有自己的亚文化。

items.meaning: a way of life opposed to the mainstream
items.meaningCN: 反主流文化（counter- 表对抗）
items.example: The magazine grew out of the counterculture.
items.exampleCN: 这本杂志源于反主流文化。

latinEntries.meaning: to prepare land, grow crops, or develop a quality
latinEntries.meaningCN: 耕作；培养（培育土地或品质）

latinEntries.meaning: a system of religious devotion or a devoted group
latinEntries.meaningCN: 崇拜；教派（敬奉体系）

latinEntries.meaning: the art of gardening
latinEntries.meaningCN: 园艺（花园＋耕种）

latinEntries.meaning: the farming of fish or water plants
latinEntries.meaningCN: 水产养殖（水＋培养）

definition_zh: 货币；通货；流通；通用；流行
definition_en: the money used in a country; the state of being accepted, current, or widely used
core_image: 一条不断流动的钱河：水在河道里跑，才叫通货
scene: 兑换柜台前，旅客拿着护照和本国纸币。 The traveller exchanged her own currency for the local banknotes at the counter.
sceneCN: 这里 currency 是「货币、通货」（第 1 个义项：一国流通中的钱）；句意：旅客在柜台把自己国家的货币换成了当地纸币。

pos.zh: 货币；通货；流通；通用；流行

senses.title: Money in circulation in a country
senses.definition: the system of money that is used and accepted in a particular country or region
senses.definitionCN: 在特定国家或地区使用并被接受的货币体系
senses.example: The euro is the currency of twenty countries.
senses.exampleCN: 欧元是二十个国家的货币。
senses.why: Latin currentia meant 'a flowing', from currere 'to run'. Money is called currency because it circulates: it runs through hands, shops and banks like water through a channel.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 currentia 意为“流动”，来自 currere“跑”。钱被称为 currency，是因为它在流通：像水在河道里一样，流过人手、商店和银行。
